notes: ⚠️ HOST EXECUTION, stated rather than implied. The tier-1 controller could not run this at all: the job declares `requires: { network: true }` for `npm install` and the approved ceiling refuses it before provisioning (#77), and — separately and more fundamentally — the job model has no form for a long-lived service alongside commands, so the probe is not expressible under it regardless of the ceiling. See the capability gap recorded as its own question. ⚠️ Controls before AND after the treatment, so 'no interference' is a comparison rather than an assertion: a second control isolates interference from any second-run effect. ⚠️ The workspace was removed and its ABSENCE checked rather than the removal call trusted — the same discipline the controller uses, applied by hand because no controller ran. ⚠️ METHODOLOGY HISTORY — AN INVALIDATED FIRST RUN, EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED FROM THE FINDING ABOVE. An earlier execution of this probe reported treatment 0/20 with the controls at 20/20, which read as total interference from `next dev`. It was a FIXTURE DEFECT, not an observation: both runs wrote the same filenames into the same directory, so the control created the files and the treatment only modified them, while the watcher listened for `add`. A second defect in the same version measured latency as elapsed-time-since-watcher-start, which reports the write schedule (20 files x 120ms) rather than detection lag and would have read as ~2.4s of latency on a completely idle watcher. ⚠️ NONE OF THAT RUN'S NUMBERS CONTRIBUTE ANYTHING HERE. They are void rather than weak, and the summary, outcome and omissions above describe only the corrected execution: a fresh directory per run, per-file observed-minus-written latency, and a control taken after the treatment as well as before. Both defects were in the fixture; neither touched the code under observation. ⚠️ It is preserved because the correction is WHY this result can be trusted rather than a detail about how it was obtained. The control is what exposed it — a result that dramatic, from a change that small, is a bug before it is a finding — and a probe whose only reported run is the one that worked has not demonstrated that it could have failed.

notes: ⚠️ TWO INSTRUMENT DEFECTS were found and corrected before these numbers were trusted, and both would have read as findings. (1) The marker extractor sliced between two sentinels in the HTML; under Cache Components the Suspense fallback ships in the static shell and the value STREAMS, so the first match landed inside escaped RSC flight data and both Cache Components runs scored 'inconclusive' while plainly serving the right value. Replaced with sentinel presence, which is immune to escaping because only one sentinel is on disk at a time. (2) The route-symbol matcher did not know `◐` (partially prerendered), so it fell through and reported `○ /_not-found` as the route under test. Both defects were in the instrument, not in Next.js. ⚠️ The baseline was re-run in the same pass as the corrected variants rather than carried over from the earlier pass, so every row here was measured by ONE instrument.
summary: Seven distinct mechanism/caching-model combinations built and served under `next build` + `next start`, each measured by writing a different value to the artifact after the server was live and re-requesting. Results: baseline/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ○ / frozen; baseline/cacheComponents:true -> ┌ ○ / frozen; connection/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ƒ / FRESH; connection/cacheComponents:true -> BUILD FAILED; force-dynamic/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ƒ / FRESH; baseline/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ○ / frozen; baseline/cacheComponents:true -> ┌ ○ / frozen; connection-suspense/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ƒ / FRESH; connection-suspense/cacheComponents:true -> ┌ ◐ / FRESH; io-suspense/cacheComponents:false -> ┌ ○ / frozen; io-suspense/cacheComponents:true -> ┌ ◐ / FRESH. Only `connection()` behind a Suspense boundary reflected the external write in BOTH caching models.

notes: ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A RE-RUN OF EVD-0023, and the difference is the point. EVD-0023 compared MECHANISMS, one read per build, to choose one. This measures the CONTRACT AS WRITTEN — `connection()` before EACH read, a fallback that is a real loading state — and it carries a NEGATIVE CONTROL inside the same build. Without the control, a fresh result would not distinguish the contract doing the work from something incidental about the build. The control was stale in both configurations, so the contract is load-bearing rather than decorative. ⚠️ THE CONTROL INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCES AST-0019 a third time, in a third instrument: `○ /bare` built static and served build-time content with cacheComponents both enabled and disabled. ⚠️ THE MIXED ROUTE IS THE FINDING NOBODY ASKED FOR. Its non-compliant read came back FRESH in both configurations, because a compliant sibling had already made the route dynamic. See AST-0022 — it is the reason the 'each read' clause is not redundant.
summary: One application, three routes, built and served twice under `next build` + `next start`. The contract route makes two planning-content reads, each awaiting `connection()` inside its own Suspense boundary with a named loading fallback. The control route makes the same read with neither. A third route mixes one of each. Copies of real planning artifacts were read through `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))` and a markdown read, then rewritten externally with the server live. With cacheComponents DISABLED the routes built as "┌ ƒ /", "└ ƒ /mixed" and "├ ○ /bare"; with it ENABLED, "┌ ◐ /", "└ ◐ /mixed" and "├ ○ /bare". In BOTH configurations the contract route served the externally written values on every request after the write, its Suspense fallback was present in the initial HTML, and the control route served its build-time values on every request including five seconds later. The mixed route served BOTH slots fresh — including the non-compliant one.
title: Experiment: the DEC-0019 read contract, with a non-compliant control on the same build

notes: ⚠️ TWO CONFIGURATION CONSTRAINTS WERE MEASURED, and both first presented as the contract failing. (1) Next.js 16.3.2 builds with TURBOPACK by default, which serialises the config — so a remark plugin must be given as a module path, not a function reference. (2) That path must be ABSOLUTE: `@next/mdx` resolves a relative path with `require.resolve(p, {paths:[projectRoot]})` from its own package directory, so `./lib/plugin.mjs` fails with `Cannot find module` and a require stack rooted in `node_modules/@next/mdx`. That message reads like a broken plugin rather than a configuration rule, and it cost a build to tell apart. ⚠️ REJECT, NOT STRIP, is what makes the diagnostics possible at all. `file.fail` carries the node's position; a stripping plugin has nothing to report because by construction nothing is wrong afterwards.

omissions.reason: `import(someVariable)` cannot be followed by a text analysis. It is DETECTED and reported as an unfollowable import, and the lint exits non-zero on one, so the blind spot is loud rather than silent — but a specifier that is computed cannot be resolved without running the code.

Only relative specifiers are resolved; a bare specifier is treated as a package. If a path alias (`@/lib/...`) is ever configured, the analyser would treat it as external and miss it. No alias is configured today.
This task covers the import boundary only. The planning-read and `<Suspense>` half is TSK-0015, and ACC-0024 needs both.

notes: ⚠️ THE FIXTURES CAUGHT TWO REAL BUGS BEFORE THE CHECK WAS TRUSTED, which is the argument for writing them first. (1) Every violation was reported ONE LINE EARLY: the pattern consumes the character before `import`/`export` so a specifier inside an identifier cannot match, and that character is usually the previous line's newline. The transitive fixture caught it because its violation is deliberately not on line 1. (2) A lazy `[\s\S]*?` let a side-effect `import "server-only";` run on to the NEXT statement's `from` clause, attributing that specifier to the wrong line and swallowing the statement between them. ⚠️ A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by a fixture: the first version scoped the check to modules REACHABLE from a route, and since no view imports the reader yet it walked two files and reported the project clean without looking at the reader or either adapter. Scope is now every module under `app/`; reachability only supplies the chain.
summary: A static analyser was built that reads application modules as text and never executes them. Run against three fixtures: the ALLOWED case (a page reaching `lib/` through an adapter) reported no violations while confirming the adapter was actually walked; the DIRECT case (a page importing `lib/` itself) was reported at `app/page.js:1`; the TRANSITIVE case (a page importing an innocent-looking helper that re-exports `lib/`) was reported at `app/_helpers/shim.js:2` — the file whose import statement is the violation — with the chain `app/page.js → app/_helpers/shim.js`. Run against the real project it reports no violations over 5 scanned modules. Falsified in real application code twice: a direct `lib/` import added to the reader was reported at `app/_read/planning.js:3` with exit 1, and a transitive one through a new `app/_helpers/shim.js` was reported at that file's line 1, also exit 1.

summary: A second static analysis was added: it scans every module under `app/`, asserts the designated reader exists and was examined, and emits four kinds of violation. omissions.reason: The CI matrix is ubuntu-latest and windows-latest. The criterion asks for Windows and THE supported POSIX platform, which this project's CI defines as Linux; macOS is not built, not tested and not claimed. A BSD-derived platform's process table and process-group behaviour are not observed by anything here.

No API can deliver SIGINT to a Windows process: `child.kill("SIGINT")` is TerminateProcess, measured — the target's handler never runs and it dies reporting SIGKILL. What an operator's Ctrl+C sends is a console control event, and CTRL_C_EVENT is undeliverable on this route because a process started from PowerShell inherits Ctrl+C disabled and a process in a new process group ignores it by definition; the Ctrl+Break handler ran and the Ctrl+C handler never did, under both Start-Process and a raw ProcessStartInfo. The Windows cell therefore observes SIGBREAK through the same handler and the same shutdown, and the SIGINT delivery itself is observed only by the POSIX cell.

The supervisor under observation is the production one and the processes, port, process table and kill mechanism are real, but the two children are fixtures: Pi needs credentials and an interactive UI, and `next start` needs a build. What this does not observe is either real program's own behaviour on being signalled — only that the supervisor performs and observes the contract against processes that spawn real grandchildren.

Both trees went within their grace periods in all four cells, so the bounded-escalation clause is exercised here only where the launcher tree needed the group kill. A tree that survives escalation is covered by unit controls over injected process tables, not by this platform run.

summary: ACC-0082's refusal and its two-part opt-in, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34397699648 at commit 7c3dde6, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 and 24, all four cells green: 776 tests, 0 failures in every cell (3 skipped on the Linux cells, 1 on the Windows cells, all platform-gated and unrelated). What the ten observe: (1) the tool checkout refuses without the opt-in, with both roots and both parts of the opt-in named in the refusal; (2) that refusal arrives BEFORE the project record is read, so a tool checkout is refused for being one rather than answered with 'run setup for this project' — setup being precisely what would create .pi/ here; (3) the flag outside the tool checkout is refused rather than ignored, with the override supplied and agreeing so the root comparison is what is under test; (4) the flag without PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR is refused, naming the variable and a value for it; (5) the flag and the override are checked AGAINST EACH OTHER — the owning directory of the named content root is re-derived and compared to the tool root, since the project root is dirname(contentRoot) and comparing only it would check that derivation against itself; (6) both parts agreeing is the one accepted arrangement, and an ordinary consumer run with different roots and no flag is untouched by any of it; (7) the opt-in GRANTS NOTHING — a self-hosting run with an invalid .pi/kiln.json still refuses project-record-invalid, which is the mutation this exists to catch, a self-host branch that skips the consumer-root checks because the operator asked for it; (8) an accepted self-hosting run completes against the production runSupervisor and announces the mode and the directory; (9) --self-host with no override reaches the SELF-HOST refusal THROUGH THE REAL COMMAND, spawned as a child process with PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR removed from the inherited environment; (10) the command line takes --self-host and refuses --selfhost, --self_host, -s, --self-host=true and a bare word. Observation 9 is the one a direct call on the helper cannot make. main() reaches resolveSelfHost only after resolveProjectRoot, and the project root is dirname(contentRoot) — so with the flag given and no override there is no content root to take the dirname of, and the command died first with the generic 'no planning content root'. That refusal answers a question the operator did not ask, about the rule they were trying to override, and its hint line does not mention the flag they typed. The checks that need only the flag and the environment therefore moved into assertSelfHostOptIn, which bin/start-kiln.mjs calls before it resolves anything and which resolveSelfHost still calls itself, so the earlier call is an ordering fix rather than the only place the rule lives. That ordering was confirmed by mutation before this run: with the assertSelfHostOptIn call removed from main(), test 9 fails; restored, it passes.

summary: ACC-0041's two sentences, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34401161647 at commit 7413055, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 and 24, all four cells green: 778 tests, 0 failures in every cell. Both of the criterion's new tests ran in EVERY cell, counted by name in each job's log rather than inferred from a green tick - the node 22 cells emit TAP (ok 702, ok 703) and the node 24 cells the spec reporter. FIRST SENTENCE, which had no test at all before this run: a real executable named `pi` reporting 9.9.9-shadow is placed first on PATH, and the measurement is two-sided. The CONTROL runs bare `pi --version` through the platform's own resolution and requires it to find the shadow; without that half the treatment would pass on a machine where shadowing was never possible, which is the failure mode of every 'we are not affected by X' test that never established X. The TREATMENT resolves the agent exactly as bin/start-kiln.mjs does and starts it with that same poisoned PATH: the started process reports 0.84.4, the shadow version appears nowhere in its output, and the resolver's own reported version agrees with the pin read from package.json. Every case-spelling of the variable is stripped from the copied environment before PATH is set, because a copied process.env on Windows can carry `Path` and a second `PATH` key beside it would leave the child resolving against whichever the platform prefers. SECOND SENTENCE: the missing-local-dependency case asserted only its reason code before this run, while the criterion asks the refusal to NAME the expected version and the resolved path. Both are now asserted twice over - in the prose an operator reads, and in a `detail` carrying `expected` and `pkgDir` so the test pins content rather than wording. DEC-0026's two values are also pinned by a test rather than left to drift: the dependency is exactly 0.84.4 and not a range, and engines.node is >=22.19.0, which is what the pinned runtime itself requires. STRUCTURE: TSK-0024 specifies lib/pi-runtime.mjs and the resolver had been written inside lib/supervisor.mjs, so the approved task described a module nobody could open. It moved verbatim to the named file, with one copy and no re-export. runSupervisor deliberately does not call it: the supervisor accepts an already-resolved command and argument array because the choice of program is the security boundary, so the consumer is bin/start-kiln.mjs, the half of the supervisor whose job is to say what runs. ONE PLATFORM DIFFERENCE, in cost rather than outcome: the PATH test costs 249ms on ubuntu/22 and 282ms on ubuntu/24 against 416ms on windows/22 and 653ms on windows/24, because the Windows control starts cmd.exe, resolves `pi` through PATHEXT to pi.cmd and then starts a second process for the batch file, where POSIX runs the `pi` script directly through its execute bit and shebang. Both routes found the shadow and both treatments reported 0.84.4, so the platforms agree on the result while differing in how they reach it.
title: Measurement: Pi resolves from the tool's own node_modules with a different pi first on PATH, both platforms through CI

summary: ACC-0057's sentinel boundary and ACC-0059's research-credential gate, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34420440250 at commit 1207ce1, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 and 24, all four cells green: 813 tests, 0 failures in every cell. All TWENTY-FOUR specialist-contract tests ran in every cell, checked by extracting each test name from the file and matching it against each cell's log in both reporter formats rather than inferring them from a green tick - the node 22 cells emit TAP and the node 24 cells the spec reporter. ACC-0057: children are spawned for real and asked which variable NAMES they can read, never values, because a test that printed values would put them in every CI log. The parent holds three sentinels named as a naive implementation would match them - ACME_API_KEY, SOMETHING_TOKEN and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, rather than a private prefix any implementation excludes trivially - plus four unselected providers' keys and the research credential. No sanitised child observed any sentinel or any unselected provider name, in any of the four cells. The POSITIVE CONTROL is what makes that mean something: a control child spawned with the environment INHERITED observed all three sentinels in every cell ('control observed 3 sentinels; sanitised children observed 0'), because a clean result is also what a parent that never held them produces. ACC-0059: the research credential is measured as a 2x2 with the key present in the host in every cell - research+enabled, research+disabled, planning+enabled, planning+disabled, validation+enabled - and TAVILY_API_KEY crosses in exactly one of them. That negative column exists only because researchEnabled is SUPPLIED rather than derived: deriving it from the credential being present would make 'the key crosses only while research is enabled' and 'the key crosses when the host has a key' one sentence. A supplied non-boolean refuses rather than reading as disabled, since "false" is truthy and the same value would have opened the gate under a truthiness check. PLATFORM RESULTS DIFFER AND BOTH ARE RECORDED. On POSIX the assertion is exact: what the child observed minus what Kiln passed deep-equals the empty list, so a Linux child receives precisely what it was given. On Windows that assertion is impossible and is not made - AST-0045 measured nine names the OS injects into every child whatever environment it is handed, and both Windows cells reported exactly those nine (HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, LOGONSERVER, SYSTEMDRIVE, TEMP, USERDOMAIN, USERNAME, USERPROFILE, WINDIR) with the 'not among AST-0045's nine' diagnostic never firing. Asserting equality there would report the operating system as a defect and bury a real leak among familiar red lines; what is asserted on both platforms is the claim that survives, that nothing credential-shaped is among what Kiln adds. The stored-route child received 4 names on each Linux cell and 14 on each Windows cell - the base list intersected with what the runner sets, plus the Pi locator, plus the nine on Windows - and no provider credential in either. Four mutations were checked locally before this run: deriving the flag from credential presence kills 2 tests, scanning the host for credential-shaped names kills 5, removing the stored fallback kills 3, and emitting a partial provider set kills 1.
title: Measurement: the child environment boundary and the research-credential gate, both platforms through CI

summary: ACC-0058's refusal, no-inference and no-scan clauses, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34418001574 at commit bb3b9cb, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 and 24, all four cells green: 799 tests, 0 failures in every cell. lib/pi-provider-credentials.mjs and its test file are byte-identical between bb3b9cb and the commit this record was written against, so the run tested the code the criterion describes. SEVEN tests carry the criterion, each checked by name in every cell's log with zero failing results, in both reporter formats: (1) T1 - an unknown provider id is refused under `unsupported-credential-contract` naming the provider, and the refusal says no name is inferred and the environment is never searched. (2) T5 - a custom declaration that fails validation makes the PROVIDER unsupported under that same reason, with the underlying problem kept in `detail.declarationProblem`, because a declaration that failed validation is not a declaration. (3) T2 - no variable name is derived from a provider id. T1 alone would not establish this: it checks what the refusal SAYS. T2 checks what the resolver DOES, against the mutation it exists to defeat - `id.toUpperCase().replace(/[-.]/g, "_") + "_API_KEY"`, which is right for about half the table. Twelve providers whose variable no such rule produces are asserted individually (moonshotai needs MOONSHOT_API_KEY, huggingface needs HF_TOKEN, github-copilot needs COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN), each first checked to be a case the deriver gets wrong so it cannot pass as a witness. The deriver's own outputs are refused as ids too: 'moonshot' is not a provider, but MOONSHOT_API_KEY exists. Replacing the table lookup with that deriver was checked locally before the run and fails 9 of 16 tests in the file as it then stood. (4) T3, structural - the module source, with comments stripped, references no `process.env` and no filesystem read or spawn. (5) T3, behavioural - with credential-shaped decoys present in the process environment, every contract serialises byte-identically to its value without them, and an unknown provider still refuses though a plausible key is now present. Both halves are needed: an implementation that scanned the environment and happened to find nothing would pass the behavioural test alone. (6) The exact declared-name table pins all 39 supported providers and the complete ordered name list of each. The membership assertions that preceded it could not see an ADDITION, which is how two Application Default Credentials variables passed a green suite and a green four-cell run on google-vertex before this commit removed them. (7) T6 - the table agrees with getApiKeyEnvVars read out of the INSTALLED @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.4, located by content rather than by the bundle chunk's build-generated file name, so a Pi version that adds or renames a provider fails here rather than being inherited by an 'audited' table. Passing on all four runners confirms the table matches what a clean `npm ci` of the pinned version ships. The criterion's remaining clause - no additional variables inherited - is not observed by this run; it is EVD-0091's, linked beside this record.

The timeout, non-zero exit, spawn failure and malformed-output paths are driven by stub children through the real parent path. What they establish is the parent's decision and its cleanup on each path, not how the pinned SDK behaves when it hangs, crashes or misreports.

Forced cleanup failure uses an injected remover - one that throws and one that returns without removing - rather than a naturally occurring filesystem failure such as a held lock or a permissions error. The detection is real, because the root's absence is verified after removal; the failure that triggers it is simulated.

The eleven mutations, including whole-file copying, were run locally before the commit and not in CI. CI establishes that the tests guarding each behaviour pass on both platforms; that those tests fail when the behaviour is broken is established only by the local runs.

summary: ACC-0104's provider canary, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34536865401 at commit b4fc232, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 and 24, all four cells green: 837 tests, 0 failures in every cell. All TWENTY-FOUR canary tests ran in every cell, checked by extracting each name from test/pi-provider-canary.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log in both reporter formats, with zero failing-test lines anywhere in any log. REAL SDK CELLS. Eleven of the twenty-four spawn the actual child, which imports the pinned @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.4, builds a ModelRuntime with allowModelNetwork false, constructs no agent session and so exposes no default tools. The six authentication and availability cells: (1) a stored api_key on a built-in provider is available with authSource `stored`, and the operator's auth.json and its directory are byte-identical afterwards; (2) an environment key on a built-in provider is available with `environment-key`; (3) a custom provider through its validated $VAR is available with `custom-environment-key`; (4) no credential is a structured unavailable refusal whose detail is exactly provider, model, available false and authSource null; (5) a stored OAuth credential on a custom provider, with its declared variable also set, is reported `configured` from `stored` while the exact model is absent - and because the source is judged first, the result is canary-auth-source-mismatch rather than a bare unavailable that would hide the undeclared route; (6) a built-in stored api_key with an empty key is `configured` from a PERMITTED `stored` source and the exact model is still absent, so the refusal is canary-model-unavailable carrying authSource `stored` - configured is not availability even when nothing else is wrong. UNSUPPORTED BEFORE SPAWN: an unknown provider refuses with the spawn function never called and no temporary root ever created. EXACT MATCHING: `claude-fable` is not `claude-fable-5`, and a real model id under a provider that does not serve it is not that model; both are unavailable. Pi's own precedence is pinned: with a stored credential and an environment key both present, Pi reports `stored`. SELECTED-ONLY STORED COPY: the operator's file holds anthropic, openai, github-copilot and acme credentials; the child's temporary copy holds exactly ['anthropic'] with that entry unchanged, and none of the three unselected credentials appears in the copy, stdout or stderr, against a positive control that the original file held each of them. A file with no entry for the provider yields a `{}` copy and a complete environment route still authenticates. A malformed file is refused as canary-stored-auth-invalid without forwarding the parser's message, against a positive control proving that on this runtime JSON.parse does quote the malformed input. AUTH SOURCE BEFORE AVAILABILITY: a forbidden source (runtime, models_json_command, fallback, models_json_key), an unknown one and a contract mismatch each keep their own refusal when the model is also unavailable; an available model with no source the runtime can name is refused as unknown. CLOSED REPORT: success is exactly {provider, model, available: true, authSource} and frozen; a child report carrying Pi's `label` of variable names is refused as canary-output-invalid rather than forwarded. SECRET AND FINGERPRINT CONTROLS: a planted credential is absent from every report, refusal message, refusal detail, child stdout and child stderr in ten forms - the value, sha256, a sha256 prefix, sha1, md5, base64, base64url, a tail, a distinctive core and the reversal - each against a positive control that it reached the child: the stored copy held it, the environment carried it, the declared variable reached the custom child. The argv is exactly the interpreter, the child, the pinned SDK entry, the provider and the model, with no --api-key and no print-api-key. CLEANUP: the temporary root is removed on seven exit paths once it exists (missing stored file, environment refusal, non-zero child, spawn failure, non-JSON output, wrong-shape output, timeout); a forced removal failure is canary-cleanup-failed on those seven paths for BOTH a remover that throws and one that returns without removing, the latter caught only because the root's absence is verified, with any earlier refusal kept as priorReason; and a refusal raised before any state exists never attempts a removal. Eleven mutations were run locally before the commit and every one fails at least one test.
title: Measurement: the provider canary confirms the exact model and a permitted auth source, both platforms through CI

summary: Supplemental to EVD-0092 for ACC-0058: the correction to provider ids that name Object.prototype members, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34540859311 at commit b648e3e, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest x node 22 (v22.23.2) and 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 840 tests, 0 failures in every cell. All TWENTY-FOUR provider-contract tests ran in every cell, checked by extracting each name from test/pi-provider-credentials.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log, with zero failing-test lines anywhere in any log. WHAT CHANGED AND WHAT DID NOT. Before b648e3e, both credential tables were read with a bracket lookup on a plain object, which also finds what Object.prototype holds. An id such as `toString` resolved to an inherited function, which is truthy, so it was refused as a DECLINED provider: detail.why held the function and the message printed its source. EVD-0092's claim that an unknown provider is refused was therefore already true for these ids - they were refused - and this record does not contradict it. What was wrong was the refusal's content, and that the same lookup in the built-in table would have returned the inherited function as a contract had the declined check not run first. Both lookups now ask Object.hasOwn, and nothing was added to the declined table. THE THREE TESTS, each passing in all four cells: (1) `F35 every Object.prototype name is refused as an ordinary unknown provider` - without a custom declaration, each name receives the ordinary unsupported-credential-contract refusal whose detail is exactly { provider }, with no `why`, plain data that survives a JSON round trip unchanged, and a message carrying no function source, no `[native code]` and no `[object`. (2) `F35 a prototype-named id with a valid custom declaration resolves like any other custom provider` - with a valid matching declaration, each name resolves to that declared contract, its id, the custom-environment-key source and the declared variable. This is what shows the fix is an own-property lookup rather than a denylist: a fix that refused these names outright would pass test 1 and fail this one. (3) `F35 the two declined providers keep their recorded reason, and built-ins resolve unchanged` - amazon-bedrock and azure-openai still carry their recorded reason, unchanged, in both detail.why and the message; the declined table still holds exactly those two ids; and every built-in provider resolves to its same frozen table entry. Three mutations were run locally before the commit and each fails tests 1 and 2: restoring the raw lookup in the declined table, restoring it in the built-in table, and the resolver exactly as committed before this correction.
title: Measurement: provider ids that name Object.prototype members are refused cleanly and resolve when declared, both platforms through CI

omissions.reason: Kiln's lock is identified by device, inode and creation time. The control showing that a lock Pi takes straight after Kiln's release is NOT reported as Kiln's leftover passed on GitHub's ubuntu-latest and windows-latest runner filesystems only. A filesystem that reports no creation time and reuses the inode immediately would compare the two directories as one. The consequence is fail-closed - a cleanup refusal, never a deletion of another writer's lock - but it is unproven outside those two runner filesystems.

The test that runs a real Pi save against Kiln's lock failed once locally, taking 18.5s against its usual 3.6s, on the run immediately after the files were edited. Its assertion text was not captured and the failure has not recurred in 14 local file runs, 10 targeted runs or any of the four CI cells. What failed is therefore unknown, and no claim is made about its cause.

The lock orders writers that take it. It cannot repair a Pi process that loaded project settings before Kiln's write and holds them in memory: Pi's save merges field by field, so a later save of a field it still holds stale - packages, for instance - would drop Kiln's entry. Setup must finish before Pi starts. Nothing here tests or claims otherwise.
The CI matrix is ubuntu-latest and windows-latest. macOS is not built, not tested and not claimed.

The 22 mutations were run locally on Windows before the commit and not in CI. CI establishes that the tests pass on both platforms; that they fail against a defect is established only by those local runs.

The merge applies whatever package entry it is given, and refuses one that is not a portable relative path. Proving that the portable spelling and the literal one `pi install -l` wrote resolve to the same package directory is TSK-0030's work under ACC-0105, and nothing here establishes it.

summary: Measurement of the settings merge through CI. GitHub Actions run 34632506490 at commit f459b2d, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 864 tests and 0 failures in every cell. ALL TWENTY-FOUR settings tests ran in every cell, checked by taking each test name out of test/pi-settings.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log, with zero failing-test lines in any log. ACC-0047, PRESERVATION AND BYTE STABILITY. A file carrying third-party packages, unrelated keys, a custom key order and unknown fields keeps every unrelated value; ordinary string keys keep their relative order; Kiln's package and skill entries occur exactly once in either Pi form, with an object entry's filters kept and only its source corrected; the trailing-newline style is kept for LF, CRLF and none, and a new file has none; applying the same desired state again returns no bytes and does not change the file's modification time, including against a file indented differently. Malformed JSON, a non-object root and an invalid value in a Kiln-owned field are refused at plan time with the file byte-identical, no lock and no temporary file, and no refusal quoting the parser, a value or a path; unknown fields, including a schemaVersion Pi does not define, are preserved rather than refused. KEY ORDER IS BOUNDED BY PI'S OWN SERIALIZER (D37): a file with integer-like property names is merged by Kiln and saved by a real Pi SettingsManager in a child process, and the two write the unrelated keys in the same order - integer-like names first in ascending order, then string keys in their textual order - at the top level and one level down, with every value intact. ACC-0048, NO SECRET AND NO MACHINE PATH. With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY planted in the environment and asserted present while the merge ran, the bytes written to .pi/settings.json in external and project mode and to .pi/kiln.json by ensureProjectId carry no credential value and no fingerprint of one - raw value, sha256, a 12-character sha256 prefix, sha1, md5, base64, base64url, the last six characters, and the value reversed - and no absolute path, drive letter, home directory or ~ reference, in raw, JSON-escaped and forward-slash spellings. Every detector is exercised against a positive control first, and the input file deliberately carries an absolute sessionDir that external mode removes. THE LOCK, PROVED AGAINST PI ITSELF. The merge takes the same proper-lockfile lock Pi takes, pinned as a direct dependency at 4.1.2, and holds it across the transaction's final identity check and its atomic replacement. A real Pi SettingsManager save in a child process, run while Kiln holds the lock, reports an error and writes nothing, and the same save succeeds once the lock is free while Kiln's fields and a third party's package entry survive it. A Pi writer that takes the lock first and writes is waited for, and Kiln refuses with CONCURRENT_EDIT rather than overwriting it; a lock Pi keeps holding is refused as settings-locked with Pi's lock left alone. The lock being held AT THE MOMENT OF THE WRITE is observed directly rather than inferred: the renameSync that puts the file in place is wrapped, and the lock directory is present at that call. CLEANUP AND A LOST LOCK (D38, A43, A44). A release that fails, or one that returns with Kiln's own lock directory still in place, is refused as settings-lock-cleanup-failed rather than reported as success, keeping an earlier refusal's CODE - never its message - as priorReason. Kiln's lock is identified by device, inode and creation time, so a lock Pi takes immediately after Kiln's release is not reported as Kiln's leftover; that control passed on both platforms. A directory created only to hold the lock is removed only while empty, so another writer's file keeps it, and a directory that cannot be removed for any other reason is refused rather than left silently. A lock lost BEFORE the merge refuses with settings-lock-compromised and writes nothing; a lock lost DURING the write - driven from inside the renameSync wrapper, after the real rename - refuses with the same code and reports the write that completed rather than rolling it back. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Twenty-two mutations of lib/pi-settings.mjs were run before the commit, each alone with the file restored byte-identical afterwards, and every one was caught: twelve on the merge and lock (no lock taken, lock released before the merge, packages replaced wholesale, keys re-sorted, trailing newline forced, no-op detection removed, owned-value checks removed, sessionDir kept in external mode, duplicates kept, portability check removed, lock-only directory not removed, contention not refused), eight on cleanup (failed release swallowed, no check that the lock is gone, presence checked instead of identity, priorReason dropped, priorReason carrying the message, every directory-removal error ignored, recursive removal, cleanup failure never refused), and two on the compromised-lock checks, each killing exactly its own test.
title: Measurement: the settings merge preserves, refuses and holds Pi's lock, on both platforms through CI

summary: Measurement of the package-entry normalisation through CI. GitHub Actions run 34635305377 at commit f3fab47, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 872 tests and 0 failures in every cell. ALL EIGHT package-entry tests ran in every cell, checked by taking each test name out of test/pi-package-entry.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log, with zero failing-test lines in any log. WHAT IS PROVED BEFORE ANYTHING IS REWRITTEN. The literal entry `pi install -l` wrote and the portable `../.planning/pi-package` spelling are each resolved from the directory the settings file lives in, which is how Pi resolves a package path. Each side must be a readable directory - statSync first - and the two canonical paths must be equal, with `.` and `..` resolved, symlinks and junctions followed, and Windows compared case-insensitively. That single comparison is the proof; an earlier device-and-inode comparison was removed as redundant, untestable on its own, and able to refuse falsely where identity reporting is unstable. SPELLINGS PROVED EQUIVALENT, on real directories: the portable spelling itself, an absolute path as `pi install -l` may write, a redundant relative path, and on Windows the backslash spelling. On POSIX the backslash spelling names nothing and is refused, because a backslash is an ordinary character in a name there. THE LINK CASE RAN ON BOTH PLATFORMS: a directory symlink on the two Ubuntu cells and a junction on the two Windows cells, each created for real, the link spelling proved equivalent, and the entry rewritten through the merge. The test reports a diagnostic and skips if a runner will not create one; no cell reported that, and nothing in that file was skipped. WHAT IS REFUSED, each leaving .pi/settings.json byte-identical with no lock and no temporary file: an entry naming another package directory (package-entry-not-equivalent), one that does not resolve or sits below a file (package-entry-missing), one that is a file rather than a directory (package-entry-not-a-directory), one that cannot be read, simulated with EACCES on exactly that path (package-entry-unreadable, carrying the errno code), an empty entry (package-entry-invalid-literal), a caller supplying its own package entry or equivalents (package-entry-already-supplied), and a missing transaction (package-entry-no-transaction). A missing package directory is refused naming the PORTABLE side, so the failure says which spelling could not be resolved. No refusal carries a path: the literal entry may be an absolute home path, and every refusal is asserted not to contain the project directory. THE REWRITE ITSELF GOES THROUGH TSK-0029's MERGE, with the literal spelling passed as an equivalent: the entry is corrected in place and occurs exactly once, third-party packages, unrelated keys, their order and the trailing-newline style are preserved, and normalising again - from the literal spelling, now absent from the file, or from the portable one - changes no bytes and does not change the modification time. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Nine mutations of lib/pi-package-entry.mjs were run before the commit, each alone with the file restored byte-identical afterwards, and every one was caught: the canonical comparison removed, paths compared as written rather than canonicalised (caught only by the link test), a non-directory accepted, unreadable treated as missing, the literal spelling written instead of the portable one, the proved literal not passed as an equivalent, a second package entry accepted, a missing transaction not named, and an empty literal accepted.
title: Measurement: the package entry is rewritten only on proved canonical equivalence, on both platforms through CI

summary: Measurement of the local-state policy through CI. GitHub Actions run 34635305377 at commit f3fab47, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 872 tests and 0 failures in every cell. ALL FIFTY-FOUR local-state tests ran in every cell, checked by taking each test name out of test/local-state.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log, with zero failing-test lines in any log. ACC-0049, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE. That a missing block refuses: `with no ignore block, project-local state REFUSES and writes nothing`. Edited: `with the block EDITED, project-local state still refuses`, which also asserts the reported state is `edited`. Partial: `partial coverage is not coverage`, where `.planning/` is ignored and the two runtime paths are not - the state an older Kiln leaves, and the one a check written as `is there a block` would pass - naming `.pi/sessions/` and `.pi/runtime/` as uncovered. Negated: `a negated rule is not coverage either`, where the rules are present and `!.pi/runtime/` follows them. THAT NOTHING IS CREATED IS ASSERTED AS ABSENCE, NOT AS A MESSAGE: each of those tests checks existsSync is false for every directory of the state layout after the refusal, and `deriving a root creates nothing, so setup can show both before the operator chooses` establishes that deciding creates nothing at all, with `creating a state root WITHOUT a lease is refused, and creates nothing` covering the unleased path. THE THREE CHOICES AS DATA: `the refusal carries the three answers, with the block's actual bytes` asserts the ids are exactly fix-ignore, user-state and stop, that the first is available, an append rather than a replacement, and carries the block's bytes rather than a description of them; `over an exact LEGACY block the option is a MIGRATION, and applying it leaves one block` covers the migration case; `over an EDITED block, 'add the block' is offered as unavailable rather than silently` covers the case where setup may not act for the operator. ACC-0050, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE. Platform convention: `the per-user home follows the convention already written down, on both platforms` and `Windows uses LOCALAPPDATA rather than APPDATA, because state must not roam`, with `a platform that will not say where state belongs is a refusal, not a guess` covering the case where the convention is unavailable. Derivation from the committed id: `the external root is keyed by the ID, not by where the project sits`, and `external mode without a committed id refuses rather than inventing one`. Separate roots for separate ids: `two projects on one machine occupy separate external roots`. The id never becoming a path component: `A TRAVERSAL ID NEVER BECOMES A PATH COMPONENT`. A root that is not outside the project being refused rather than used: `EXTERNAL STATE MUST BE PROVED EXTERNAL, not assumed from the mode's name`, `the coverage exemption re-proves it, because it is reachable on its own`, `A CHILD JUNCTION CANNOT REVERSE WHAT THE ROOT PROVED`, and `a project the external root would write INTO is caught, which the root check alone cannot see`. The committed record: `the id lands in the committed record, and the record is exactly what the schema permits` asserts the keys are exactly projectId and recordVersion; `NO COMMITTED FILE HOLDS AN ABSOLUTE USER PATH` asserts the bytes carry no drive letter, /home/, /Users/, AppData or XDG reference, and not the project's own path; `the project id is minted once, and only through a live lease` and `an INVALID record is a recovery decision - never repaired, never a second identity` cover minting and recovery. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY, AND ONE SURVIVED. Nine mutations of lib/local-state.mjs were run against the suite, each alone with the file restored byte-identical afterwards. Eight were caught: the coverage refusal removed (8 tests), uncovered paths reported but called covered (8), the external exemption granted by the mode's name (7), the project id not checked before it becomes a path component (1), the external root not keyed by the id (3), a platform that says nothing guessed at (1), the state root created without a lease (9), and an invalid record read as though it were valid (1). ONE SURVIVED, and it is recorded as an omission rather than smoothed over: removing `assertKnownMode` from `coverageState` changes no test result, because every test that exercises an unknown mode reaches it through `stateRootFor` or `createStateRoot`, which refuse first. That guard's own comment says it was added because a mode misspelled the same way in two places once fell through to the permissive branch, so it is exactly the kind of default-deny that should not rest on where its callers happen to check.
title: Measurement: the coverage gate creates nothing and the external root derives from the committed id, both platforms through CI

summary: Supplemental to EVD-0097 for ACC-0049 and ACC-0050: the two gaps that record named, now closed, observed on both platforms through CI. GitHub Actions run 34642326014 at commit 76d5254, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 874 tests and 0 failures in every cell. ALL FIFTY-SIX local-state tests ran in every cell, checked by taking each test name out of test/local-state.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log, with zero failing-test lines anywhere. EVD-0097 stands as recorded; nothing in it is withdrawn. GAP ONE, THE UNKNOWN-MODE GUARD. EVD-0097 recorded a surviving mutation: removing `assertKnownMode` from `coverageState` changed no test result, because every test that passed an unknown mode reached `stateRootFor` or `createStateRoot`, which refuse first. The new test `DECIDING COVERAGE refuses an unknown mode itself, rather than through whoever called it` calls `coverageState` directly with seven misspellings - projcet, PROJECT, Project, ' project', 'project ', 'user ' and anything - each passed in the layout as well as in the request, so the binding check that compares them is cleared and the call reaches the guard. THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT TEST DID NOT KILL THE MUTATION EITHER, and that is the finding worth keeping: `assertLayout` refuses an unknown mode a few lines later with the SAME refusal code, so asserting the code alone passed with the guard deleted. The test now asserts which check refused - the refusal's `detail.what` is `Deciding coverage`, and `detail.mode` is the value passed - and the mutation dies. A shared refusal code can hide a missing guard. GAP TWO, THE READ-FAILURE BRANCH AND WHAT A REFUSAL CARRIES. EVD-0097 recorded that the test named for an unreadable record wrote malformed JSON, leaving the branch that reports a record which cannot be READ with no test. That test is renamed to `a record that is not JSON is invalid, not absent`, which is what it exercises, and a new test forces EACCES at exactly the record path, with the raised error deliberately carrying both the record's absolute path and a credential planted in the file. The record is reported INVALID rather than ABSENT - absent invites minting a second identity for a project that already has one - and the refusal is inspected AS A WHOLE: name, reason, message and detail serialised together, asserted to contain neither the planted secret, nor the project directory, nor the record's absolute path, nor the OS error text, each checked raw, JSON-escaped and with forward slashes, because on Windows those are not the same bytes. What it does carry is asserted positively: detail is exactly { path: '.pi/kiln.json', detail: 'cannot be read (EACCES)' }. THE REFUSAL ITSELF CHANGED TO MAKE THAT TRUE. It quoted the OS error message, V8's parser output - which quotes the file's own bytes around a syntax error - and the record's absolute path, in both the message and the detail. It now names the record by its stable relative identifier and reports the errno code alone. `projectRecordState` still returns the absolute path, which is what a caller acting on the file needs; no caller read the refusal's.
title: Measurement: the coverage guard refuses in its own name, and the record refusal carries no machine path, both platforms through CI

omissions.reason: A lock is only held while its holder can say so. proper-lockfile renews a lock from a timer every half of the stale window, so a holder that is suspended, descheduled, or blocking its own event loop past that window has abandoned it by the library's contract, and another writer may take it and write. This is the same contract that lets Kiln recover from a Pi process that died holding the lock, so it cannot be closed from one side. It is recorded in lib/pi-settings.mjs as an operational property and is deliberately NOT asserted by a test: a ten-second timing test would buy nothing but a slow suite.

The probes that measured the takeover - event loop blocked for 8s, 10.5s and 12s, and free for 12s - were run locally on Windows against the pinned proper-lockfile and Pi's own nested copy. They are not part of the suite and did not run in CI. CI establishes that the corrected control passes on both platforms; the takeover threshold is established only by those local probes, on one platform.

Neither of the two local failures was captured: the first was lost to a filtered command and the second never recurred while being watched. The mechanism above fits both - each ran far past the stale window while every passing run sat near 3.8s - but which assertion failed in those two runs is unknown and is not claimed.
The CI matrix is ubuntu-latest and windows-latest. macOS is not built, not tested and not claimed.

summary: Supplemental to EVD-0095 for ACC-0047: the control that proves a real Pi save cannot write while Kiln holds the settings lock, re-observed after that control was corrected. GitHub Actions run 34646036685 at commit 962e8dc, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 880 tests and 0 failures in every cell, with all TWENTY-FOUR pi-settings tests matched by name in every cell and zero failing-test lines anywhere. EVD-0095 stands as recorded and nothing in it is withdrawn. WHAT THE OLD CONTROL DID, AND WHY IT WAS REPLACED. EVD-0095's contention control started Pi's save with `spawnSync`, which blocks the event loop for the whole lifetime of the child. `proper-lockfile` keeps a lock alive by touching its directory from a timer every half of the stale window, and a blocked loop runs no timers - so while that control ran, Kiln could not renew the lock it was holding. On a loaded machine the child sometimes took longer than the ten-second stale window, at which point Kiln's lock was abandoned by the library's own definition and Pi's `lockSync` took it over and wrote. The test failed twice locally on that path, at 12.2s and 18.5s against a usual 3.6s, and its output was not captured either time. The claim EVD-0095 recorded was never shown false - every CI cell it cites passed - but the control was proving less than it appeared to: a process that cannot renew its lock is not the same as two writers cooperating. WHAT THE CONTROL DOES NOW. The child is spawned asynchronously and awaited, so the event loop stays free and the lock is renewed on schedule while Pi runs. The assertions are unchanged: Pi's own SettingsManager, in a child process, reports an error and writes nothing while Kiln holds the lock; the bytes either side of that save are identical; and once the lock is free the same save succeeds while Kiln's fields and a third party's package entry survive it. The test now runs in about two seconds rather than four, and passed in all four cells here and in three consecutive local runs. THE MECHANISM WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Two probes were run locally against the pinned proper-lockfile and Pi's own copy. With the event loop BLOCKED while Kiln held the lock: Pi was refused with ELOCKED at 8s, and took the lock over at 10.5s and at 12s, removing Kiln's directory and writing. With the event loop FREE for 12s: the lock directory had been touched 2.0s before the check and Pi was refused with ELOCKED. That is the difference the correction makes, and it is the reason the flake is gone rather than merely absent.
title: Measurement: the real-Pi contention control, re-observed with a lock that can be renewed while Pi runs

Twenty-two of the supervisor's existing cases supply an already-approved reader and an agent directory that is never opened, because they are about readiness, shutdown, ports and stdio rather than about trust. The gate's own behaviour rests on the nine gate tests, of which two use the real store, plus the three harnesses that now pass the real gate.

Two module tests inject a `storeFactory` rather than using Pi's store: one counts instances to show a write is verified by a SECOND one, the other makes every later reader disagree so the not-persisted refusal can be observed. The cycle itself is pre-existing and was not restructured in this task; what is established is that the gate's default still lives in the gate and cannot be omitted by a caller.

A differently cased Windows path is a DIFFERENT key, because Pi keys its store on realpathSync(resolve(cwd)) and that keeps the case it was handed. Kiln matches Pi rather than folding case: a Kiln that normalised case would stop matching decisions Pi itself records through its own prompt. summary: Measurement of the project-trust integration through CI. GitHub Actions run 34652112338 at commit 203c4ed, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 899 tests and 0 failures in every cell, with zero failing-test lines in any log. ALL NINE trust-gate tests and ALL TEN trust-module tests ran in every cell, checked by taking each test name out of test/supervisor.test.mjs and test/pi-trust.test.mjs and matching it against each cell's log. THE STORE, AND THE BOUNDARY DEC-0027 DREW. lib/pi-trust.mjs reads, grants, denies and revokes through `ProjectTrustStore` as exported from the pinned package's ROOT, resolved by the same pinned resolver the CLI uses. A structural test asserts the module names no trust file, writes no file itself, reaches no inner package path, and knows no default agent directory. Three states are kept distinct: `missing` is a project nobody has been asked about and `denied` is an answer the operator gave, asserted both as states and in what the record names. Every write is read back through a SECOND store instance and refused as `trust-not-persisted` if it did not land - provable only because a `storeFactory` seam lets a test make a write appear not to land, which the real store will not do on request. THE KEY IS PI'S OWN RULE. The project directory is canonicalised before every operation with `realpathSync(resolve(cwd))`, which is what Pi's `normalizeCwd` does, so a trailing separator, a `.` and a `..` that comes back all share one decision and a denial through one spelling replaces the decision rather than sitting beside it. THE GATE, AND WHERE IT SITS. runSupervisor asks before anything else it does: the ordering is proved by which refusal arrives, since a project with no `.pi/kiln.json` and an unusable PORT still refuses on trust rather than with `no-project-record` or `port-invalid`, and the `spawn` supplied throws if it is ever reached. `trust-missing` and `trust-denied` are separate codes with different remediation - decide, or change a decision - and both name `bin/start-shell.mjs` in the message and in the detail. A refusal leaves the committed record, the ignore block and the contents of `.pi` byte-identical, and creates no runtime directory. ONE AGENT DIRECTORY, ASKED OF PI AND FORCED DOWNWARD. `resolvePinnedAgentDir` asks the package's root-exported `getAgentDir()` rather than restating Pi's home-directory rules; bin/start-kiln.mjs calls it once, in the process whose environment the children inherit, and runSupervisor requires the answer rather than defaulting one - a run without it refuses `agent-dir-missing` having consulted no store at all. That exact value is what the gate reads the store with, and it is forced into every child as PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, replacing a stale inherited spelling; both children are asserted to carry it. The Ubuntu cells resolved their POSIX home-derived directory and the Windows cells their Windows home-derived one, and every cell passed the assertion that the value used for the lookup is the identical value handed to the children. TWO CASES RUN THE REAL STORE, NOT AN INJECTED ANSWER, in every cell: an approval granted through lib/pi-trust.mjs reaches the existing launch path and completes the ordinary shutdown contract, and a denial recorded the same way stops the run with the refusal naming the directory it was recorded against. THREE EXISTING HARNESSES NOW RUN THE REAL GATE and still pass in every cell: the stdio-routing fixture, which spawns a real supervisor in its own process, and both shutdown-evidence harnesses, natural and interrupt. Each grants trust through the real store in a temporary agent directory, so what they measure is the production path rather than one with the gate removed. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Nine mutations of the gate and the resolver, and ten of the module, were run before the commits, each alone with the file restored byte-identical, and every one was caught. Two of them survived their first attempt and are worth recording: moving the gate after the project record passed until a test existed whose project had no record, and asking the gate with the raw spelling passed until the test used a spelling `join` does not collapse.
title: Measurement: trust is read and recorded through Pi's exported store, and an unapproved project never starts an agent

summary: Measurement of Kiln's Pi package through CI. GitHub Actions run 34656876359 at commit e162336, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 912 tests and 0 failures in every cell, with zero failing-test lines in any log. ALL NINE package-validation tests and ALL FOUR real-load tests ran in every cell, matched by name against test/pi-package.test.mjs and test/pi-package-load.test.mjs. THE PACKAGE AS AUTHORED. `pi-package/package.json` declares one extension file, one skills directory and one prompts directory; every declared resource exists; the entry point loads and exports a registration function; and `signature.json` - authored separately and never derived - declares signatureVersion 1 with extensions [kiln], skills [kiln-planning], prompts [kiln-start] and tools [], deeply frozen and asserted to survive a JSON round trip. The entry point states signature version 1 for itself, a third independent statement, and a mismatch between any two is refused. Refused as well: an absolute or backslashed manifest path, a path climbing out of the package, one path declared twice or under two kinds, a declared resource that is not there, an extension suffix Pi does not load, a declaration naming a resource the package does not have or omitting one it does, a name that is a path, and a repeated name. Importing the entry point reads nothing outside the package, writes no file, starts no process and contacts nothing - asserted in a child whose watchers are then shown to see a read, a write and a spawn the child makes deliberately. THE PACKAGE AS PI LOADS IT. Each load case builds an isolated project and agent directory, copies only `pi-package/` into `<project>/.planning/pi-package/`, writes `packages: ["../.planning/pi-package"]` into `.pi/settings.json`, and asks the pinned runtime's own DefaultResourceLoader what it discovered. No provider is configured, no credential exists, no model request is made and no child process is started. TRUSTED, THE EXACT SETS: one extension, resolvedPath `<project>/.planning/pi-package/extensions/kiln.js`, sourceInfo.source `../.planning/pi-package`, scope `project`, with zero tools, zero commands and zero handlers registered and no load errors; skills exactly kiln-planning (project, at `skills/kiln-planning/SKILL.md`) and the control; prompts exactly kiln-start (at `prompts/kiln-start.md`). Compared as exact sets with exact paths, because an `includes` check would pass against a package that also loaded something nobody declared. THE TWO NEGATIVE CASES, EACH WITH THE SAME CONTROL. With no decision recorded, and with an explicit denial, the extension does not load, the prompt is not discovered, the project skill is not discovered, and there is no error - while a user-scoped skill in the agent directory, which project trust does not gate, IS discovered. That control is what makes the empty result mean discovery ran and the package was not loaded, rather than the run having exited early. THE ENTRY POINT IS IMPORTED, NOT MERELY NAMED, AND THAT IS WHAT ANSWERS THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS. Deleting `signature.json` from the copied package produces exactly one load failure, reported against `extensions/kiln.js` and naming that import - so Pi follows the JSON import attribute (F63). Appending invalid JavaScript produces exactly one load failure against the same path with a parse error - so Pi parses and imports that exact `.js` file rather than reading the manifest alone (F61). In both, the package's skill and prompt are still discovered, which places the failure in the module rather than in the package. A fourth case asserts the file that loaded is the one `pi.extensions[0]` names. PLATFORM DIFFERENCE: COST ONLY. Every assertion held identically on both platforms and both Node versions. Windows runs each load case roughly three to four times slower than Ubuntu - the trusted case 68.7ms against 21.0ms, the entry-point controls 194.6ms against 57.2ms - which is filesystem cost for copying the package and building four fixtures, not a behavioural difference. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Eighteen mutations were run before the commits, each alone with the file restored byte-identical, and every one was caught: twelve against the manifest, the declaration, the entry point and the validator, and six against the loaded package - the manifest naming a different extension file, the skill renamed, the prompt renamed, the entry point registering a tool, the entry point no longer importing its declaration, and the manifest pointing `prompts` at another directory.
title: Measurement: the package declares what it owns, loads under trust, and is absent without it

They are how the registry is read, how a model resolves without anyone's endpoint, how the session is driven and finished, and how startup network operations are disabled. The pinned entry point and the --tools policy are production's, unmodified; nothing here claims the interactive TUI path was exercised.

The reading is taken on session_start, and no model turn occurs. What a later turn would hold is not measured, and nothing in the run calls setActiveTools - so a mid-session change of the active set is outside what this establishes.

None is reachable from an argument or an environment variable, and the real command still selects both programs internally - but each is a place where a test observes a shape production assembles.

The wrapper replaces anything that looks like an absolute path with <path> rather than parsing it. That is deliberate - a message can carry a path as prose, and the cost of missing one is disclosure - but it means a result's prose can lose a fragment that merely resembled a path, and the tests assert absence rather than fidelity of what remains.

summary: Measurement of Kiln's Pi tool registration through CI. GitHub Actions run 34699903816 at commit 60e4fe0, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 961 tests and 0 failures in every cell, one attempt, no job retried, and zero failing-test lines in any log. WHAT RAN, BY NAME, IN EVERY CELL. All 5 session-measurement tests (test/pi-session-tools.test.mjs), all 31 wrapper tests (test/pi-package-tools.test.mjs), all 15 package-validation tests (test/pi-package.test.mjs), all 4 package-load tests (test/pi-package-load.test.mjs) and all 80 supervisor tests (test/supervisor.test.mjs) were matched by name against their source files in each of the four cells - 540 name matches, none missing. ACC-0064: WHAT THE SESSION ACTUALLY HOLDS. The production launch composes the agent as withToolAllowlist(resolvePinnedAgent(TOOL_ROOT), await piToolAllowlist(TOOL_ROOT)), which appends `--tools` and one comma-separated value naming the 22 declared tools to the pinned bin.pi entry point - the form Pi parses, since dist/cli/args.js matches `--tools` or `-t` and splits the NEXT argument on commas. That composition is read back out of the real command: a child runs bin/start-kiln.mjs with its supervisor replaced by a recorder and reports the argument array main() built. The measurement itself spawns that pinned entry point against an isolated project holding a copy of pi-package/ named through `packages: ["../.planning/pi-package"]`, trusted in a temporary ProjectTrustStore, and reads pi.getActiveTools() and pi.getAllTools() from inside the session on session_start. The reading is the session's own registry - not signature.json, not the registration recorder, not the `--tools` argument, and not the tool definitions in a provider request, which are four different claims. Measured active set: exactly the 22 declared names. Measured configured set: the same 22. All eight of the pinned runtime's built-ins - read, bash, powershell, edit, write, grep, find, ls, extracted from its own allToolNames rather than restated - are absent from both. TWO CONTROLS, BECAUSE EACH READING WOULD OTHERWISE BE COMPATIBLE WITH A BROKEN INSTRUMENT. The same probe, in a session launched without the allowlist, sees read, bash, edit and write active alongside the Kiln tools, 26 in total - so their absence in the measured run is Pi applying the flag rather than the probe being blind. And the same probe, over an untrusted project, sees no name beginning kiln_ at all while Pi's own tools stay active and the session still exits 0 - so the 22-tool difference is package discovery, and the empty Kiln set is a refusal to load a project's package rather than a run that never built a registry. ACC-0065: WHAT EACH WRAPPER DOES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. Twenty-two tools are registered from three explicit tables and four direct registrations: nine creations over TYPED_TOOLS, eight mutations over MUTATION_TOOLS with a per-row call adapter because the eight operations do not share a signature, activation over PROJECT_TOOLS with the tool root it needs to validate reachability, two stage-attestation operations over lib/attestations.mjs, and the two reads over the lint and the handoff gate. No wrapper allocates an id, validates a field, takes a lock, writes a file or restates a trace rule: each resolves the project through the shared resolveContentRoot and delegates. Every handler is asserted against real artifacts read back from disk - evidence linked into supportedBy and withdrawn, the same for refutedBy, a revision that changes one field and reports which, a lifecycle retired, a question answered with its answer recorded, a trace target added and removed, a review status moved, an activation that rewrites one manifest line while its comments survive, and an attestation written and read back per stage. REFUSALS CHANGE NOTHING, AND SAY SO AS DATA. Ten mutation refusals, four activation refusals and five attestation refusals were each taken with a bytes-and-modification-time snapshot of the whole content root before and after: every file identical, none rewritten or touched. Refusals are returned rather than thrown, with a code from the error's own class - invalid-artifact and artifact-exists for artifacts, invalid-request for activation and attestations, which are not artifacts and would send a model looking for one to correct. Results and refusals carry no credential and no machine path: checked against a planted key and against every spelling a path can reach a JSON result in, since JSON.stringify doubles a backslash and a check that knows one spelling is blind on Windows. THE DECLARATION AND THE REGISTRATION AGREE EXACTLY. signature.json declares 22 names at signatureVersion 1; running the registration function with a recording stub produces exactly those 22; and validatePackage refuses a package where the two differ in either direction, where a name is registered twice, or where the entry point states a different signature version. The launch allowlist consumes that validated set rather than reading the file, so a name reaching the command line is one the package proved it registers. PLATFORM DIFFERENCE: COST ONLY. Every assertion held identically on both platforms and both Node versions. The four real sessions take 340-453ms each on Ubuntu and 830-939ms on Windows, about 2.5x, which is process-spawn cost rather than a behavioural difference. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Thirty mutations were run before the commits, each alone, from a temporary working directory, with the file restored byte-identical: six against the read wrappers and the creation tools, ten against the mutation tools, ten against activation and the attestations, eight against the launch allowlist, and seven against the session measurement. All were killed except one - weakening the exit assertion itself, which cannot be detected while the behaviour is correct, and whose killing mutation is the session killed rather than asked to finish.

omissions.reason: No successful Tavily request was made through the Pi wrapper. Every successful research path in these tests used a stand-in backend; the production route that ran in CI was the real Tavily adapter refusing as no-credential before any network access. Whether a live search through the wrapper succeeds against the real backend is not established here.

A complete validation run with a real Python interpreter was observed locally only, on Windows with Python 3.12.10: a job exiting 0 in about 4.4s and a failing job exiting 1 in about 4.2s, both with the workspace destroyed and nothing leaked in the rendered results. CI does not set up Python, so no cell provisioned a virtual environment or executed a real job; the CI routes use node as the interpreter and an unresolvable PATH.

The validation controller deliberately retains precise internal paths - workspace, interpreter, retained directory, a job's own output - as diagnostics for its own callers, and those values exist in its results. The Pi wrapper is the disclosure boundary and suppresses them in what a model receives. A consumer that bypassed the wrapper would see them; none exists today.

After the exact workspace root and the known machine roots, a general absolute-path scrub replaces anything path-shaped with <path>. That is deliberate - the cost of missing a path is disclosure - but it means a job's output can lose a fragment that merely resembled a path, and the tests assert the absence of machine paths and the survival of chosen content rather than full fidelity of everything else.

Most adapter tests supply the implementation through register(pi, deps) - stand-in research backends, node as the validation interpreter, forced cleanup behaviour, recording wrappers around the real controller. These seams model the production boundaries rather than being them; the production wiring itself is exercised only through the no-credential and unresolvable-PATH routes, and the seam is not reachable from Pi, an argument or an environment variable.

The thirty-three mutations were run locally on Windows before the commits. CI establishes that these tests pass on both platforms; that they fail against these defects is established only by those local runs.

F82: on Windows and Node 24 the pinned runtime can abort in RPC mode when shutdown begins within 50ms of a second-or-later turn. The real-session kiln_capability test therefore stops the child once the agent settles and makes no claim about its exit status, and no CI cell enters that window, so this harness cannot observe F82 on any platform.
