summary: Measurement of TSK-0047's consumer skill override through CI. GitHub Actions run 34760917147 at commit 13e074e, attempt 1 with no job retried, matrix ubuntu-latest x windows-latest by node 22 (v22.23.2) and node 24 (v24.20.0), all four cells green: 1011 tests and 0 failures in every cell, zero failing-test lines in the log. The skills check printed clean in every cell, and the live Pi compatibility step on ubuntu-latest node 24 ran 5 tests and passed 5. WHAT RAN, BY NAME, IN EVERY CELL. All 3 tests in test/stage-skill-overrides.test.mjs - "kiln-stage-01-intake through Pi's real loader: packaged only, override present, override edited, override skill removed", "control: an absent override directory is silently ignored, and the packaged skill loads", "control: an untrusted project loads neither the package's skills nor the override, while the user-scoped control still loads" - were matched by name against the source file and passed in each of the four cells, 12 matches, none missing, failed or skipped. The 15 package-validation, 4 package-load, 11 generator, 11 command and 4 packaged-output tests also passed by name in every cell. THE ENTRY IS KILN'S. Each fixture is an isolated temporary project holding a copy of pi-package/ at .planning/pi-package, an override directory at planning-content/skills-overrides holding only .gitkeep, as the initializer scaffolds it, and a .pi/settings.json that is exactly the output of mergeSettingsText for a fresh project with Kiln's package entry. The test asserts that the merged settings hold exactly skills ["../planning-content/skills-overrides"] and packages ["../.planning/pi-package"]; it never spells the override entry itself. PI DOES THE LOADING, FRESH FOR EACH STATE. Every observation constructs a new DefaultResourceLoader from the pinned runtime, with the fixture as its working directory and a fixture agent directory, and calls reload() with Pi's non-interactive trust rule composed from its root exports. No provider is configured, no credential exists, no model turn is taken and nothing touches the network. HOME is pointed at an empty directory inside the fixture for each load and restored afterwards, so Pi's ~/.agents/skills scan cannot add the runner's own skills to the exact sets. THE FOUR STATES FOR kiln-stage-01-intake, EACH ASSERTED EXACTLY. (1) Packaged only: the loaded filePath is <project>/.planning/pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md, the parsed description is the packaged one - stated from stages/01-intake.json in the generator's wording, not read back through Pi's parser - and Pi reports no collision. (2) Override present: exactly one skill with that identity loads, its filePath is <project>/planning-content/skills-overrides/kiln-stage-01-intake/SKILL.md, its description is the override's, and Pi reports exactly one collision, for that identity, with the override file as winner path and the packaged file as loser path. (3) Override edited: the same override filePath loads with the edited description, and the same single collision. (4) Override skill removed while the override directory and the settings file remain - the directory's existence and the settings bytes are asserted - the packaged filePath and packaged description load again and Pi reports no collision. In every state the loaded set is exactly the other nine packaged skills, each from <project>/.planning/pi-package/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, plus the identity and the user-scoped control from the agent directory, and Pi reports no other skill diagnostic. CONTROLS. With the override directory deleted and the settings entry still naming it, the packaged skill loads with its packaged description, the full set is unchanged, and Pi reports no collision and no diagnostic of any kind: an absent override directory is silently ignored, not refused. With no trust decision recorded, and again with an explicit denial, and an override present, the only skill loaded is the user-scoped control from the agent directory - none of the package's skills and not the override - and nothing collides. PLATFORM DIFFERENCE: NONE IN OUTCOME. Every assertion held identically on Windows and Ubuntu under node 22 and 24. Only durations differed: on node 24 the four-state test took about 298 ms on Windows and 50 ms on Ubuntu. WATCH ITEMS. F89 did not recur: all eight shutdown evidence records were complete with nothing unobserved and no shutdown-not-observed refusal. F45's real-Pi-save test, F50's slice 5c and port-retry tests, and all 5 R7 readiness tests passed in every cell, with no bad port or fetch failed in the log. MUTATION CONTROLS, LOCAL ONLY. Eight controls were run against the test file, each alone from a temporary working directory, restored byte-identical, with the repository's git status and fingerprints of pi-package/ and planning-content/ unchanged and no fixture left behind. Killed: the override entry removed or misspelled in the merged settings (caught by the merged-settings assertion); the entry removed or misspelled only in the file on disk (caught by the override-present loader assertion); the override's frontmatter identity changed (caught by the override-present loader assertion); and one loader reused across states and reloaded once (all three tests failed). Name-only assertions passed on the correct fixture and let the changed-identity defect survive, which the full assertions kill. The first harness run used only the merged-settings mutations and paired name-only with one of them; both were caught before any loader assertion, so the on-disk mutations were added and the name-only control was rebuilt around the changed identity.

omissions.reason: Two consecutive green runs do not prove the WMI provider cannot stall again. Priming moves its first use before the children exist and bounds it at 10,000 ms; it does not make the provider fast. Recorded as mitigated, with the standing rule that another primed timeout in CI removes WMI wholesale in favour of a WMI-free identity format.

No CI run has exercised a refused launch: every preflight so far verified. The refusal paths, a timeout, a failing reader, a table without this process, and a row with no creation time, are covered by unit controls over injected readers and by mutations MP3 to MP5, not by a platform run.

The cold preflight was measured at 3,142 ms and 3,057 ms on two CI runners and at 333 to 347 ms locally. That is four observations, not a distribution, and nothing here bounds how slow a cold provider can be short of the 10,000 ms refusal.
The 73 mutation controls ran locally on Windows against node v24.18.0, not in CI.
The CI matrix builds ubuntu-latest and windows-latest only. A BSD-derived platform's process table and process-group behaviour are not observed by anything here.

Carried from EVD-0088: no API can deliver SIGINT to a Windows process, so the Windows cell observes a real CTRL_BREAK_EVENT through the same handler and the SIGINT delivery itself is observed only by the POSIX cell.
Carried from EVD-0088: the supervisor, processes, port, process table and kill mechanism are real, but both children are fixtures. Neither real program's own behaviour on being signalled is observed.
Carried from EVD-0088: every tree went within its periods in these runs, so a tree surviving escalation is covered by unit controls over injected process tables rather than by a platform run.

summary: For ACC-0081, and it records what EVD-0088 could not have shown. FOUR FAILED MEASUREMENT RUNS CAME FIRST. Run 34849329259 refused the windows-latest node 22 natural shutdown twice, on the attempt and its one re-run, with shutdown-not-observed, both trackers at clean 0 and unresolved 1, no identity reads and about 2,720 ms spent. Run 34901223783, the first with per-query records, showed a windows-22 query taking 3,573 ms and completing 364 ms after the agent exited: its table held the agent's own row and the real child, and it was discarded as raced, so the run refused. Runs 34955664251 and 35028709582 showed the severe form on windows-24 natural, where both trees' first queries exceeded the 10,000 ms process-table timeout at 10,126 and 10,159 ms, then at 10,249 and 10,078 ms, their successors were still unresolved when the shutdown finalized, nothing was enumerated, and the run refused at about 2,740 ms. Run 34910936533 is R18's source: green, yet recording spentMs 8092 against an 8,000 ms budget with withinBudget false, passed by an evidence-test ceiling this criterion never stated. ATTRIBUTION RUN 35055338147 SETTLED THE CAUSE. Each query was recorded in phases. On windows-22 natural the first query cost 7,266 ms: 13 ms to start the child, 7,114 ms waiting for its first byte, 138 ms draining; on windows-24 natural 3,388 ms, as 18, 3,230 and 140. Every later query in those runs answered in about 300 ms. Both trees' first queries emitted their first byte in the same millisecond though they began 450 ms apart, and a WMI-free Toolhelp32 probe run beside them read the same machine in 68 ms and 45 ms, returning the same row count. The cost is neither machine load nor process creation: it is one shared first use of the WMI provider. THE GREEN RUN IS 35086096358, all four cells, 1,141 tests and no failures in each. The launch preflight ran and verified on all six Windows records, at 3,142 ms and 3,057 ms on the cold natural runs and 375 to 435 ms on the warm interrupt and enumeration runs, reading 148 to 153 rows, and recorded ran false with reason not-windows on all six POSIX records. The first tracked query after priming cost 827 ms on windows-22 natural and 483 ms on windows-24 natural, against 7,266 and 3,388 ms unprimed. All twelve records report complete true, withinBudget true and unfinished empty, spending 5,817 to 6,697 ms of 8,000 on Windows and 5,105 to 6,238 ms on Linux, and the whole run contains no process-table-timeout, shutdown-not-observed, descendants-unverified, identity-changed or creation-time-ambiguous marker. MUTATION CONTROLS RAN LOCALLY: 73 mutations across six sets, O14 MP1 to MP9, O12 MD1 to MD18, O11 MT1 to MT14, F119 MQ1 to MQ12, F116 MI1 to MI16 with 14 active, and O8 MS1 to MS6, each applied one at a time from a temporary working directory, every one killed, with lib/supervisor.mjs restored byte-identical, git status back to baseline and no fixture directory left behind. Locally on Windows the preflight measured 333 to 347 ms and the first query after it 319 to 349 ms, with the real evidence tests passing 4 of 4 in each of two isolated runs.
title: Measurement: enforced shutdown deadline and bounded Windows launch preflight

summary: For ACC-0103, and it is about WHICH session ran, never that one did. THE IDENTITY IS PROVED BY THE ARGUMENT PI WAS INVOKED WITH, matched against what is on disk. A first run mints one v4 id, records it and passes it as --session-id, which creates the session it names; a rerun passes the recorded id and the record still names the same session. Both are asserted twice over, with a generator that never repeats, so a freshly minted id could never coincide with the recorded one. F121 CAME FIRST AND WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE PINNED 0.84.4: Pi stores sessions as <timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl and keeps the id in each file's header, a different value from the uuid in the name, so a file named ...11111111-... reports id 99999999-...; deriving ids from filenames reported every real recorded session as gone. Ids now come from SessionManager.list through the package's root export, and the directory is inspected first because list answers 0 for an absent directory, a regular file and an empty one alike. F128 WAS MEASURED THE SAME WAY. --session-id for a session that has gone prints a warning and creates an empty session with that id; --session <file> for a missing file silently becomes a NEW session with a RANDOM id; --session <id> exits 1 without creating anything, and preserves the header id and the prior messages, which the stub-model probe confirmed by the history sent on the next turn. So a resume passes --session <id> and a first run passes --session-id. THAT IS NOT EXACT ON ITS OWN: Pi lists and then opens in two steps and falls back to a prefix match, so a resume also loads Kiln's guard, which at session_start compares the bound id, the transcript's canonical path and the digest of the bytes Kiln inspected. Eight ways of stopping Pi were measured in a real console: ctx.shutdown() deferred until idle and let a whole turn run, signals and process.exit left the cursor hidden, and an uncaught throw from a microtask reached Pi's crash handler, which restored input mode 503 and the cursor and exited 1 with no provider request, no transcript write and no input processed. End to end against the real CLI: a matching session continued with 1 provider request; a changed transcript and a mismatched id each stopped it with 0 requests and the verdicts transcript-changed and session-id-mismatch. FOUR SHAPES PI REWRITES WHILE OPENING were measured and are refused before spawn — an older or missing header version, an unterminated last line, an empty file, and a branch without a message or a thinking level — each changed on disk before session_start, while a current transcript did not. RECOVERY ASKS AND NEVER GUESSES: the list is numbered with no id and no path, nothing is preselected, and an empty line, a closed input, an interrupt, q, or three answers that mean nothing all cancel with nothing spawned and nothing recorded; without a terminal the run refuses with the command for each shell. A choice is written only under the session lock and only while the record's bytes, the listed sessions and the chosen session all still hold. THE FINAL RUN IS 35294728144, all four cells, 1,203 tests and 0 failures in each, with the nine S2 tests and the nine F128 tests passing in every cell. MUTATION CONTROLS RAN LOCALLY, SET BY SET. Discovery and the record, MR1-MR9: 9 active, 9 killed. The launch, MS1-MS7: 7 active, 6 killed, MS4 equivalent because a resume's minted id is discarded by the re-plan under the lock. The plan's position and the picker's rendering, MV1-MV12: 12 active, 12 killed. The transcript refusals and the preflight record, MX1-MX13: 13 active, 13 killed. The guard file, MG1-MG10: 10 active, 8 killed, MG2 and MG5 NOT EXECUTED because this host has neither POSIX mode bits nor the privilege to create a file link. The resume launch, MH1-MH8: 8 active, 8 killed. The recovery, MS2a-MS2i: 9 active, 9 killed. summary: Adaptive question selection and continuous intake capture, proven deterministically in CI and then by one retained real-model pair judged by a person (TSK-0049, against ACC-0069 and ACC-0113). DETERMINISTIC, CI RUN 35378594390 AT COMMIT 673d203, four cells green, no job re-run: windows-latest node 22 and node 24, 1239 tests / 1238 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped each; ubuntu-latest node 22 and node 24, 1239 tests / 1230 pass / 0 fail / 9 skipped each. Zero `not ok` lines in any cell. THE WRITER (ACC-0113). `kiln_write_stage_document` is the only writer for a stage document's intake section, registered in the package and declared in signature.json. It appends one entry to each of two anchored regions: the operator's answer stored as the exact input string, and, separately, what Kiln took from it. Payloads are length-framed by UTF-16 code-unit count, so an answer containing an anchor, a label or a code fence is stored rather than obeyed; labels must run A1..An in both regions, so the next label is never taken from the highest number a payload contains. Thirteen tests in test/stage-documents.test.mjs cover 20 hostile answers round- tripping, the placeholder replaced once, the astral-character measure, dynamic fence length, concurrency under the lock with no temporary file left, and the initializer's own output being writable. REFUSAL OUTSIDE THE CONTENT ROOT'S STAGE DOCUMENTS (ACC-0113). Eight refusal codes, each leaving the document byte-identical, asserted over bytes and modification times: invalid-request, stage-document-outside-root, stage-document-missing, stage-document-unreadable, stage-document-anchor-missing, stage-document-frame-invalid, stage-document-entries-invalid, and the wrapper's tool-content-refused and no-content-root. A stages/ directory replaced by a junction out of the root is refused, not followed. Refusals are classified by class rather than by the writable `name`, proven by an impostor error carrying that name and one of the writer's codes. The block is built newest- first from the whole parse and bounded at ten entries, 1 KiB a field and 16 KiB of JSON measured after cleaning, so the newest answers stay visible after stageOneDocument.text is cut from the front at 64 KiB. THE CANONICAL RULE (ACC-0069). stages/01-intake.json declares `questionSelection`, and lib/stage-skills.mjs carries every declared line verbatim into kiln-stage-01-intake, contributing only the heading and four labels. The rule names the sequence after an answer - record through the writer, lint, re-read the status, ask one question - and forbids a fixed list, a repeated question, a compound question and a proposed solution. /kiln-start now sends the fresh turn to that rule instead of restating one, and keeps its no-solution and no-mutating-tool instructions. Declaring the rule defers the choice of next ACTIVITY still: stages 02-09 keep their sentence byte for byte, so all seven of TSK-0071's fields remain undeclared on every stage. THE DETERMINISTIC PAIR. test/pi-package-project-status.test.mjs drives one project copied byte-identically, records the same interpretation in both and differs only in the operator's answer: orchestration, blockers, ready, artifactCount and project are deep-equal while `intake` differs. test/pi-package-tools.test.mjs runs the declared sequence in order against a real project and asserts the status it ends on carries the answer. THE RETAINED REAL-MODEL PAIR, attempt 2, 2026-09-18, reviewed by the project's PM. Requested and resolved both openai-codex / gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning medium, asserted from each transcript's own model_change and thinking_level_change records before any behaviour was read. One session was run through the first question and archived; each branch is that archive restored to the same path, verified byte-identical to it and to each other, and answered once. The shared first question was 'What do you want this project to accomplish for the port office?'. Branch A answered 'We keep losing the reasoning behind decisions.' and branch B 'Onboarding a new engineer takes three weeks.'. Both called kiln_write_stage_document with the answer byte- exact, then kiln_lint, then kiln_project_status, which returned intake state `recorded` with that entry; both then asked exactly one question. A: 'Which decisions in the dock-fee reconciliation process most need their reasoning preserved?'. B: 'What outcome do you want for the three-week onboarding period?'. The reviewer confirmed for both branches that the writer received the exact wording, lint followed the write, the status followed lint and returned the updated intake, exactly one question was asked, the questions differ, each responds to its own branch's recorded uncertainty, neither repeats an answered question, neither is compound, neither proposes a solution, neither asks about Kiln internals, wording stayed separate from interpretation, and no direct file-edit tool was available or used. ATTEMPT 1 WAS A FAILURE AND IS NOT SUPPORTING EVIDENCE. It ran openai-codex / gpt-5.5 with thinking off, which was not the specified configuration, so it is an invalid measurement as well as a failed behavioural attempt: one branch never called the writer, its intake never changed, and its second question came from conversation memory. It is retained as a failed predecessor and is cited nowhere as support.

summary: The operator-only boundary on attestation, artifact approval and type activation, proven deterministically in CI and then in one real Pi RPC session where the dialog was never answered (TSK-0050, against ACC-0070). DETERMINISTIC, CI RUN 35395591003 AT COMMIT bd4a2af, four cells green, no job re-run: windows-latest node 22 and node 24, 1277 tests / 1276 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped each; ubuntu-latest node 22 and node 24, 1277 tests / 1268 pass / 0 fail / 9 skipped each. Zero `not ok` lines in any cell. THE GATE. `ctx.ui.confirm` is called with `{ signal, timeout: 30000 }`, the signal being the tool invocation's own rather than the agent's, and only a literal `true` authorises the act. No UI context, rejection, cancellation, timeout, abort and an unexpected UI error all refuse and all write a bounded refusal record; they share one code, `operator-confirmation-not-granted`, because Pi returns the same `false` for every one of them and its own timed-confirm example labels the outcome "Cancelled or timed out". The confirmation is read and discarded inside the invocation that asked for it. NO AUTHORISATION REACHES A TOOL ARGUMENT. `decidedBy` and `approvedBy` left the model-facing schemas and `reviewedBy` was never in one; with `additionalProperties: false` an invented parameter is refused by the schema. The actor supplied to the libraries is the package's own constant, `operator via Pi UI`. Attestation persists it as `decidedBy` and activation persists it in the manifest; review status persists the approved status and stores no approver, because the artifact envelope has no reviewer field, and neither the criterion nor the dialog claims otherwise. Only `approved` is gated on review status, which is the word this criterion uses; `draft`, `in-review` and `amended` pass through deliberately. THE AUDIT FILE. `state/operator-boundary-refusals.json`, newest 100 entries, each holding occurredAt, operation, code and a target of validated identifiers and enums only. A target field that does not match its pattern is dropped rather than stored or escaped, so no path, argument, reason, operator or model wording, credential or transcript content can enter; a record whose target cleans to nothing is still a record. An existing file this module could not have written is refused rather than replaced. Every way the record can fail is one typed error, the lock included, and a refusal that cannot be recorded still refuses, under its own code `operator-boundary-refusal-unrecorded`, with the storage error never reaching the model. OBSERVABLE IN RECORDED STATE. `kiln_project_status` carries a closed `boundaryRefusals` block with states recorded, empty, absent and invalid, the newest ten returned beside total and omitted. A corrupt audit file reads `invalid` and does not refuse the status call. THE REAL RPC SESSION, 2026-09-18, reviewed by the project's PM. One real Pi session in `--mode rpc`, offline, with the package loaded and the 29-name allowlist; the provider is a loopback server scripted to call `kiln_write_stage_attestation` and then `kiln_project_status`, and the harness never writes a dialog response. Pi emitted one `extension_ui_request` at 833 ms with `method: confirm` and `timeout: 30000`; no response was sent; the refusal `operator-confirmation-not-granted` reached the model 30,058 ms later. The attestation file existed before the run holding an unrelated entry and was byte- and mtime-identical afterwards, sha256 be97f5265178ef98 at 199 bytes both times. The audit file did not exist beforehand and afterwards held exactly one entry, operation `write-stage-attestation`, target stageId `01-intake` and criterion `request-understood`. The `kiln_project_status` call that followed returned that entry to the model with state `recorded`, total 1, returned 1, omitted 0. The session settled with no error.

summary: The material-change rule, delivered on every turn in CI and followed in four retained real-model records (TSK-0050, against ACC-0115). DETERMINISTIC, CI RUN 35395591003 AT COMMIT bd4a2af, four cells green, no job re-run: windows-latest node 22 and node 24, 1277 tests / 1276 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped each; ubuntu-latest node 22 and node 24, 1277 tests / 1268 pass / 0 fail / 9 skipped each. DELIVERY. The rule rides the stage-context frame, which is rebuilt on every `before_agent_start`, because /kiln-start is read once on the fresh turn and a stage skill is per-stage content a consumer may override wholesale; neither governs every later turn. It is prepended in one place, so it reaches all three of the frame's outcomes - a current stage, every stage complete, and failing closed - exactly once and always ahead of the `<stage-skill>` block. Its six required sentences are asserted independently of the constant: state the proposed change in a turn of its own, stop and wait for the operator, call the mutating tool only after the reply approves it, treat rejection, cancellation and no reply alike as no call, exclude `kiln_write_stage_document` because it records the operator's own answer, and let a stage skill add to the rule but not relax it. An override writing the opposite rule into its own skill still receives Kiln's rule first and unmodified, with its own bytes delivered whole. No prompt, no generated stage skill and no stage definition restates it. Feeding each outcome's prompt back to the hook in the project state that produced it returns it byte for byte, with one frame and one copy of the rule. In a real session against a live provider the frame received opens with the rule, exactly once, with the stage line immediately after. THE RETAINED RECORDS, 2026-09-18, reviewed by the project's PM. openai-codex / gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning medium, requested and resolved identically and asserted from each transcript's own model_change and thinking_level_change records before any behaviour was read. One session was run to the operator's request - record a decision that dock fees will be reconciled nightly - and archived at 135 files; each branch is that archive restored to the same path, verified byte-identical to it, and answered once. NO REPLY. The shared first turn stated the proposal - a decision titled "Nightly dock-fee reconciliation", recording that dock fees will be reconciled nightly rather than on demand because the port office needs same-day figures - and made no tool call at all, mutating or otherwise, leaving every file under planning-content unchanged. That is the no-reply proof: the turn ends with nothing pending, so until the operator supplies another turn nothing happens. APPROVAL. Answered "Yes, approved. Go ahead and record it.", the branch created DEC-0001 with the proposed title and statement; data/decisions/DEC-0001.json and .ids.json were added and nothing was changed or removed. REJECTION. Answered "No. Do not record that decision.", the branch made no tool call and changed no file, and said so. CANCELLATION. Answered "Cancel this. Do not record anything.", from the same preserved first-turn snapshot as a required fourth record rather than a rerun, the branch made no tool call and changed no file, and replied "Cancelled. Nothing was recorded.". THE APPROVAL BRANCH'S FOUR ATTEMPTS ARE A LIMITATION, NOT A FAILURE. It called kiln_create_decision four times to produce one artifact; three were malformed and Kiln's schema boundary refused them, writing nothing and consuming no id, so the counter reached 1. All four came after approval and all four targeted the approved decision, and only the proposed mutation reached disk.

The wire value `task-not-delivered` is unchanged, so nothing that switches on the code had to move. The old name asked whether something arrived down a channel the design deliberately CLOSES - the child is spawned `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` - which read as a contradiction and invited a later implementer to reopen stdin to satisfy it. A repository-wide sweep finds no remaining `stdinDelivered` or `NO_STDIN` outside the comment recording the move. THE PAIRED ASSERTION. Either half alone is misleading: closed stdin says only that a channel was shut, and an arrived task alone leaves open that it arrived down the forbidden one. THE OBSERVATION POINT. `sentinelReachedProvider` is computed from a recording provider's log of the request the child's own model turn produced, so it is evidence from OUTSIDE the child. The verifier tests `!run?.taskBindingObserved`, so only a literal `true` passes: `undefined`, `null`, `false` and a missing field are each refused, and a mutation accepting any truthy or merely-defined value is killed. summary: One real pinned-Pi child per CI cell, launched by the production delegation runtime, measured for its selection, its tools, its role, its task, its binding and its cleanup (TSK-0053, against ACC-0076). EVIDENCE STRENGTH, STATED RATHER THAN BLENDED. A REAL PINNED-PI CHILD covers two paths and only two: a successful run and a run the provider never answers, which the bounded timeout must end. Every other path - a refused binding, an abort, a failed launch, a surviving workspace, a throwing remover, an unconfirmed teardown - is covered by DETERMINISTIC TESTS against a scripted child, because those states cannot be produced reliably from a real one. CI RE-RAN THE LOOPBACK MEASUREMENTS AND CONTACTED NO REMOTE PROVIDER: the child talks to a loopback HTTP server on 127.0.0.1, so no credential, no cost and no network variability enters, and nothing here is evidence about any real model's behaviour. THE MUTATION SETS RAN LOCALLY, NOT IN CI, on Windows only. THE RETAINED RUN, IN ALL FOUR CELLS. `test/delegate-real-child.test.mjs` spawns the pinned agent against a loopback provider and asserts six facts from one run. The child's reported provider, model and thinking level equal the orchestrator's - `kiln-loopback`, `loopback-model`, `medium` - taken from the child's own live context, never from a flag the parent set and never inferred. Its active tool set equals the intersection of the research role's declared allowlist with the measured host registry, exactly eight names: research_capability, research_fetch, research_search, kiln_create_assertion, kiln_create_evidence, kiln_create_question, kiln_link_evidence, kiln_unlink_evidence. Six built-in tools are asserted absent. The provider receives the canonical `specialists/research.md` as the system prompt, compared byte for byte, with all seven of its sections present and Pi's own coding-assistant prompt proven gone. It receives a task-scoped payload: exactly one user message carrying the framed task, and no parent conversation. stdin is closed. The binding is observed. Temporary material is removed and the tree is confirmed stopped. THE LAUNCH PROTOCOL WAS CORRECTED AFTER MEASUREMENT, NOT BEFORE. A first real run showed the provider receiving Pi's generic coding-assistant prompt, no role definition at all, and no `tools` key whatsoever - the child was told it was a coding assistant and offered nothing, and the gate refused it as `capability-missing`. The protocol now passes `--no-extensions --no-skills --no-context-files --no-builtin-tools --system-prompt <role>` and loads exactly two explicit extensions, Kiln's package and the task-binding observer, in that order. THE CHILD REPORT (D46). Pi's native JSON events were measured and report the provider and the model on assistant messages but NOT the thinking level and NOT any tool name; the `session` event carries `{type, version, id, timestamp, cwd}` alone. A second typed line on fd 3 therefore carries what the child holds - provider, model and thinking level from its live context, active tools from its live registry, and signatures reduced to the two fields the contract compares. The binding attestation is unchanged byte for byte and the two lines are routed by type. A missing, duplicated, malformed, unsorted, out-of-bounds or contradictory report yields no signatures at all, so the gate refuses. TWO DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT BEFORE ACCEPTANCE AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH. (1) RAW-STDOUT DISCLOSURE: the runtime returned the child's whole event stream as its answer, and Pi's `agent_end` event echoes the user message - so the framed task, its nonce and its digest travelled back inside the delegation's own result. The retained real-child test caught it; the runtime now returns the text of the last assistant message. (2) NUL SEPARATOR: `lib/specialists/child-report.mjs` joined tool names on a literal U+0000 to compare sortedness, which is invisible in source and made git treat the file as binary. A comma is sufficient because the name pattern admits no separator, and the reason is recorded in the file. F130 IS RECORDED AS NOT RECURRING, NOT RESOLVED. `A8 each companion is a separate process` passed in every cell of this run, at 1.30 s on windows-latest node 24, and has passed in every cell of the last several runs. Its cause was never established beyond the phase evidence pointing at PowerShell process startup rather than reflection emit or the native query. This task spawns child processes under a bounded timeout, so the areas overlap, and it remains a watch item.

CI RE-RAN THE LOOPBACK MEASUREMENT AND CONTACTED NO REMOTE PROVIDER: the real child talks to a loopback HTTP server on 127.0.0.1, so nothing here is evidence about any real model's behaviour, and nothing here is evidence about what a specialist DOES with a task it accepts. The child exits zero, its task binding is observed true, its report lists zero active tools, and the delegation refuses `capability-missing`. Its prose is not returned and the refusal carries no `output` field at all. F39 the binding now refuses at its own step rather than at `verifyChild`, so a child that was never given the task is never refused for a wrong model instead. summary: Every canonical stage definition declares the seven fields ACC-0112 names, the loader refuses one that omits or malforms any of them, every generated stage skill carries them from its definition, and the check fails by name when the two drift apart (TSK-0071). FIVE THINGS ARE SHOWN SEPARATELY, BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF FACT. (1) THE NINE AUTHORED DEFINITIONS. Each of `stages/*.json` gained `purpose`, `method`, `nextActivity`, `delegations`, `mutationBoundary`, `approvalBoundary` and `completionSummary` - 117 leaf slots across nine files, 516 added lines and no deletions. The content was drafted from the existing definitions, the generated skills and the repository's own recorded decisions, and reviewed as a nine-by-seven matrix before anything was written. Where a source did not settle the wording, the gap was named rather than filled, and four of those gaps were then settled as NEW canonical instructions (D57-D61) rather than presented as facts recovered from older artifacts. (2) THE LOADER'S REFUSALS. `lib/stages.mjs` refuses a definition that omits a field, gives it an unknown key, empties a list that must not be empty, repeats an entry, leaves a sorted list unsorted or puts a line break inside a line. Three vocabularies are checked rather than trusted: activities must be a duplicate-free SUBSEQUENCE of a semantic order, so a stage cannot claim it exits before it authors; a delegation's capabilities must EQUAL its role contract's, sorted and unique, and are never derived from it; `mayMutate` names canonical non-creation operations, so a wire name or a creation is refused. Two permissions are iffs rather than implications, because either half alone would let a definition say a thing in one place and unsay it in another. Every refusal names the stage and the field. (3) THE GENERATED SKILLS. Each skill carries all seven under six headings, with `approvalBoundary` and `mutationBoundary` sharing `## Boundaries`. The headings and two labels are the generator's; every substantive line is the definition's, asserted value by value including each delegated capability by name. An empty declaration renders as exactly `[]` and nothing else. The `## Not in this skill` section, which existed only to announce that these fields were undeclared, is gone. (4) THE DRIFT CHECK. Thirteen cases change one field to another loader-valid value, leave the generated file untouched, and assert `checkStageSkills` reports exactly that skill stale. summary: The drift half of ACC-0092, for TSK-0067. The code is commit 7c3b8a1, and CI observed it at d927151. The presence half is ACC-0109 on EVD-0106, where a real loaded session calls kiln_capability and receives the shipped signature.json unchanged. That declaration lists tool names only, so it cannot show a parameter-schema change. This record observes the schemas themselves. WHAT RAN. The Pi compatibility spike builds a clean consumer with its own npm install and resolves the pinned CLI from it. It copies the shipped Kiln package from tracked files into two projects inside that consumer, records trust for each through ProjectTrustStore, and names the package in each project's .pi/settings.json. In one project the package is unmodified. In the other, the copy of pi-package/extensions/kiln.js has research_fetch's schema changed to add a property kilnDriftProbe and make it required. The spike refuses to continue unless that change lands exactly once. Each project runs a real Pi session in rpc mode with --no-session and --offline, answering one get_state query. WHERE IT WAS OBSERVED. An observer loaded with -e reads Pi's live registry at session_start through pi.getAllTools(), reduced by the product's own buildChildReport from the consumer's copy of lib/specialists/child-report.mjs. It also keeps research_fetch's raw parameters. All three research-role tools are taken from that reading, and none is supplied by the harness. THE CONSUMER AND ITS EXPECTED SIGNATURE. verifyChild(contractFor("research"), run) judges each reading. The expected signature is contractFor("research").toolSignatures from lib/specialists/contract.mjs, which the run does not edit, and the retained assertion checks that it does not carry the drift property. The package declares its research schemas in its own table in kiln.js, so the change moves only the observed side. Task binding observed, not timed out, and a fixed output string are held constant as test inputs. No task was delegated and no Kiln child was launched. THE POSITIVE CONTROL. On both platforms the unmodified session exited 0, answered its state query, reached session_start and loaded the package. All three research tools matched the expected signature, and verifyChild accepted the run and returned the output. THE REFUSAL. On both platforms the drifted session exited 0, answered, reached session_start and loaded the package. Pi's registry held research_fetch with properties url, maxBytes and kilnDriftProbe and required [url, kilnDriftProbe]. verifyChild refused the run as signature-mismatch and did not return the output. research_capability and research_search still matched, so the refusal is attributable to research_fetch alone. BOTH TIERS APPLY ONE ASSERTION. assertContract() in test/pi-compat.test.mjs checks the pinned version, both observation points, exit status, the answered query, package loading, the full research tool set from the registry, the unmodified acceptance, the changed schema in the registry, the refusal and its attribution, and the unedited expected side. It also re-judges both retained readings with the current verifyChild, so a later change to the consumer is tested against what Pi actually held. summary: TSK-0065, toward ACC-0090. LINUX ONLY: every run is WSL Ubuntu 24.04 under script(1), which gives Pi a pseudo-terminal. Nothing here says how Pi behaves in a Windows terminal. WHAT PI OFFERS. Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch (F7). `pi auth` offers only check, print-api-key and print-bearer-token, and /login exists only as a slash command inside the interactive TUI. The check therefore launches the full TUI. THE LAUNCH, FIXED FOR EVERY RUN. The pinned CLI from a clean clone at 061a706, with --no-session --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve --offline, an environment of exactly HOME, LANG, PATH, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and TERM, and HOME, the agent directory and the working directory each a fresh temporary directory. PATH holds Node's directory and the system binaries only. THE NO-TTY CONTROLS. The same launch, with stdin and stdout varied, each stopped at 20 s by timeout, with Pi's exit and elapsed time taken inside the Pi stage. With both streams a terminal, the TUI rendered and was still running at the timeout (exit 124, 20.1 s). This is the mode control: it shows the probe sees the TUI when it is there. With stdin /dev/null, Pi exited 0 in 0.3 s and printed nothing. With stdout a pipe, Pi exited 0 in 0.2 s and printed nothing. With stdin an open pipe, and with both streams pipes, Pi was still running at the timeout (exit 124). In none of the four did the TUI render. Those runs are not the interactive mode. That Pi selected print mode in them is read from its source (resolveAppMode in dist/main.js) and agrees with what was observed, and the waiting runs agree with Pi reading an open stdin pipe until it closes (F8). No no-TTY case refused: two exited 0 silently, and two waited until stopped. THE INTERACTIVE RUN. An operator at a real terminal typed /login, chose Sign in with an API key, selected OpenAI and pasted a throwaway key generated by the harness, which works nowhere. Pi reported 'Saved API key for OpenAI', and the operator exited. Pi exited 0 after 36.8 s. The TUI rendered, and Pi read the operator's keystrokes while the harness read nothing from stdin. AUTH, ASKED SEPARATELY. Before the run, pi auth check --provider openai --json --no-refresh exited 1 with not_ready and credentials_not_configured. After it, the same check exited 0 with ready, openai, api_key. The isolated auth.json held one openai entry of type api_key, and it held the key that was entered. This confirms locally configured authentication. It does not show the key works against OpenAI, and account authentication belongs to TSK-0066. F13: PI DISPLAYS THE KEY. The key prompt shows the pasted key in plain text, unmasked, and the transcript captured it on every redraw. It appeared three times: twice in the key prompt, and once where the operator first pasted it into the provider search box. Anything that logs or tees the terminal during /login records the key. F14: A SESSION MODEL WAS SELECTED. After saving, Pi printed 'Selected gpt-5.5' and the status line changed from unknown to gpt-5.5. This run did not compare Pi's settings before and after, so it does not establish whether that selection was persisted. F15: the success message prints the absolute path of the credentials file. KEY ABSENCE. The harness generated the key, removed every occurrence from the transcript, and refused to save the record or the transcript if any 8-character run of the key's random part survived. Both were saved, so neither held one. The key and any fingerprint of it were discarded with the run. test/pi-compat-login.test.mjs cannot know the key, so it does not prove its absence. It checks the pin, the launch arguments, the environment names, each control's mode and bounded outcome, the interactive exit, auth before and after, the stored shape, the redaction scan on all four files, that no hex run of 16 or more survives, and that the transcript's redaction markers match the recorded redaction count. summary: TSK-0034, toward ACC-0054, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit 2ea341a, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. lib/consent-record.mjs reads the ignored consent record under the existing consent schema before any prompt, and lib/connection-inspection.mjs gains inspectWithConsent, which reuses a recorded inspection answer and asks only a host with none. WHAT GRANTS. A record grants only when it is valid, its location passes the existing coverageState check, and Git gives a definite answer that no clone can carry it. gitProtection runs from the record's own directory, so Git finds the repository that really holds it (the project, a parent repository, a linked worktree whose .git is a file, or a nested repository), and asks three things: whether the record is in the index, whether it is in HEAD, and whether that repository's effective rules ignore it (git check-ignore). Only ignored, or no repository at all, lets the record be trusted or written. Tracked, committed, not ignored and inconclusive all grant nothing, and a record in any of those states is never written over. Writes ask even when the file is absent. Missing, unreadable, invalid and unprotected records grant nothing. THE THREE GRANTS. Inspection, model use for one exact provider and model, and research use for tavily are written, read and cleared separately. Only true or false is recorded. A closed input or empty answer grants nothing and records nothing. INVALIDATION. Whenever a read sees a current choice different from the one a grant names, or no choice, the grant is removed from the record under the lock, so model A to B to A asks again, and research tavily to none (or unset) to tavily asks again. clearGrants is the call a choice writer makes in the same step. HOW IT IS OBSERVED. test/helpers/access-recorder.mjs, the harness of EVD-0125, watches Pi's agent directory on the second host and the credential variables ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY, and makes every network call record and throw. The second host holds a stored openai key in auth.json and sentinel values in the environment. Counts are taken at every prompt and after every credential access, so each prompt is compared with the state just before it. CLONE CONTROLS. (1) PROJECT-LOCAL STATE: the first host grants all three and an unchanged relaunch asks nothing. The project is committed, git ls-files shows exactly .gitignore and .pi/kiln.json, and git clone produces the copy. On the second host the record is absent, and all three prompts reopen with zero credential access before the inspection prompt and none added before the model-use or research prompts. (2) PER-USER STATE: the clone derives the second host's own root from a different LOCALAPPDATA and XDG_STATE_HOME. The record there is absent and the same prompt sequence holds. Git reports no repository for the per-user root. (3) THE POSITIVE CONTROL, in every clone control: after each yes, the recorder sees the auth.json read, the model-use credential read and the research credential read, so the zero counts at each prompt are absences rather than blind spots. No network attempt was recorded. NEGATIVE CONTROLS. (R1) A valid, fully granted record force-added past the ignore block and committed reaches the clone inside the ignore rules. It is read as tracked and grants nothing, all three prompts reopen before any credential access, the answers are not written, and the file bytes are unchanged. (R5) After git rm --cached without a commit, the first host reads the record as committed and refuses to write it. A clone of that HEAD still receives the granted record, which grants nothing there, with the same prompt sequence. The first host trusts its record again only once the removal is committed. The linked-worktree test asserts the same, then asserts the record is trusted after the committed removal. (R6) A project with no .git of its own inside a parent repository that does not ignore it: an answer is not written there (reason not-ignored, with no file created), and a granted record placed there by hand is not trusted. After the parent runs git add -A, commits and is cloned, the clone receives the record and it grants nothing, with the same prompt sequence. A parent repository that ignores the runtime directory lets the record be written and reused. OTHER TESTS. Unchanged local reuse, recorded declines, non-answers, separate grants, provider-only changes, a model choice removed, explicit clearing, and a choice that omits model or research being refused so a grant cannot be cleared by omission. LIMITS. (R4) Where Git is unavailable or gives no definite answer, no saved answer is trusted and none is written, so an unchanged project is asked on every launch. The answer's result carries notRemembered, which tells the operator the answer applies to this run only and why. This was tested with a missing Git binary. (R7) Protection is checked against the current checkout on each read. A checkout of another branch is checked against that branch's HEAD, and older commits are not examined. (R2) The invalidation and clearGrants behaviour is proved at the API. No choice writer exists yet: the model selection writer (TSK-0036) and the research choice writer (TSK-0035) must call clearGrants when they change a choice, and nothing yet shows they do. (R3) A second clone on the same machine for the same user in per-user state shares the local record keyed by the committed project ID. That is the same operator on the same host, and ACC-0054's case is a machine with no local record. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. The launch path and the choice writers are not connected, so ACC-0054 is not evaluated here. No real model or research request was made: the credential uses in the controls are reads of the variable. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Five changes each failed the tests: inspection standing always granted, inspection before the prompt, the index check removed from the read, the HEAD check removed, and not-ignored treated as safe. summary: TSK-0035, toward ACC-0054, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit 7115a56, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. lib/research-enablement.mjs adds the Tavily step of setup and the research choice writer. lib/consent-record.mjs gains reconcileGrant and peekGrant, which judge one choice-keyed grant by its own choice so that the research step, which does not know the model selection, cannot clear a model-use grant. THE STEP. Inspection's presence result decides whether anything is asked. Absent gives no-credential and not-inspected gives user-disabled, and neither asks, reads the key or writes. With the key present, the separate approval uses the section 6.5 prompt verbatim, or --research tavily stands in for it. The first read of the key is the adapter's GET /usage probe, after the answer. Only an available probe persists anything: the project choice tavily in .pi/kiln.json through the setup transaction, and this host's grant in the consent record. The decision is made with peekGrant, which changes nothing, so a stale grant (a Tavily grant beside a project with no research choice) stands as ask and needs fresh approval, but is removed only by a successful enablement. A decline is persisted: a project with no choice takes none, and a project where another operator committed tavily keeps it while this host's decline is recorded. A non-boolean answer grants nothing and writes nothing. Every path returns an outcome, so declining never blocks planning. OUTCOMES. available, no-credential, authentication-failed, quota-exhausted, backend-unreachable and user-disabled carry the section 6.5 wording, with remaining credits only when Tavily reports them. Every user-disabled result carries a hint naming --research tavily. THE WRITER. writeResearchChoice clears this host's research grant before writing the choice, so a crash between the two leaves the old choice with no grant, which only asks again. Disabling always succeeds: when the grant cannot be cleared (Git cannot verify the record, or it is tracked), the write to none still goes ahead and reports the grant as uncleared. Every write back to tavily requires a successful clear first and is refused without one, with the reason in plain English. HOW IT IS OBSERVED. The real createTavilyAdapter is given an environment Proxy that counts reads of TAVILY_API_KEY and a fetch that records every request and answers as Tavily would. Counts are taken at the prompt. RESULTS. (1) Approval before use: zero key reads and zero requests at the prompt, then exactly one GET /usage (the positive control), available with 988 of 1000 credits, tavily committed and the grant recorded. An unchanged rerun asks nothing and probes again. (2) Failed probes: 401, 403, 429, 432, zero credits, a network error, a 500 and the key gone each give their own outcome and write neither file. (3) STALE GRANT (D4): with no research choice and a stale Tavily grant, approval is asked with zero key use at the prompt, and after a 401, a 429 and a network error both kiln.json and the consent record are byte-identical. The absent and not-inspected paths also leave the record byte-identical, and a successful probe then replaces the grant. (4) ROUND TRIP: tavily to none through the writer removes the grant, none to tavily through the writer revives nothing, and the next setup asks with zero key use at the prompt. (5) Clear before write: a concurrent edit that makes the merge refuse still leaves the grant cleared and the choice unchanged. (6) D1, WITH GIT UNAVAILABLE AND WITH A TRACKED RECORD: disabling succeeds through the writer and through --research disabled, and the record that cannot be cleared is left byte-identical. Enabling through the writer or --research tavily is refused and changes nothing. Once the record can be cleared (Git available, or the removal committed), enabling clears the old grant first and the next setup asks. (7) Declines are remembered in both scopes, --research disabled writes none without reading the key, and neither file holds the key. (8) A research-only reconcile leaves the model-use grant in place. LIMITS. After a disable that could not clear the grant, the grant stays in the record until a later Kiln write to tavily clears it. A change back to tavily made outside Kiln, such as a checkout, once the record is trusted again is not seen by the writer, and a read that sees the tavily choice would then find the grant. That is the observation limit recorded in EVD-0126. The model selection writer (TSK-0036) and the launch path are not connected, so ACC-0054 is not evaluated here. summary: TSK-0036, toward ACC-0055 and ACC-0054, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit af8259e, which corrects 2dd4930's thinking-level check, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. lib/model-selection.mjs chooses, confirms and persists the project's model, and records this host's model-use grant. CHOOSING. The choices are exactly the models a granted inspection listed, by provider display name and exact model ID, with nothing marked as a default. A choice is a number the operator typed, or --provider and --model checked against that list. Pi's global default is never read, and the first entry is never taken: an empty answer, q, 0, a number off the list, a non-integer, a name or a closed input cancels with nothing written. No thinking level is assumed; it comes from --thinking or an answer. THINKING LEVELS ARE THE MODEL'S. 2dd4930 checked --thinking only against Pi's global level list, and pinned Pi clamps a level the model does not support, so the confirmation could promise high while Pi ran at off. af8259e takes the supported levels from Pi's own getSupportedThinkingLevels, imported from the pi-ai the pinned agent resolves (resolvePinnedCompat), applied to the registry's model after inspection consent with allowModelNetwork false. Only supported levels are offered interactively, an unsupported --thinking is refused before any confirmation or write, a committed level the model does not support is not reused, and a model whose support Pi cannot report is refused. CONFIRMING. Every selection is confirmed, including a single listed model whose ID looks like an alias (kiln-latest). The prompt names the provider display name and ID, the exact model ID and the thinking level, and states that intake turns and specialist work will run on it using this computer's connection, may consume billable tokens or provider quota, and that the account, limits, pricing plan and charges are the operator's. Only true is a yes. A run that cannot ask refuses, even with valid flags. PERSISTING. On a yes to a changed selection, this host's model-use grant is cleared first, the exact provider, model and thinking level are merged into .pi/settings.json through applyKilnSettings (DEC-0028), and the grant is recorded for exactly that provider and model. If the grant cannot be cleared, the change is refused before anything is written or granted. A committed selection, as another operator or a Pi login (F14) may leave it, is offered for confirmation on a host with no grant and never used on the strength of the file. RESULTS. (1) Single model: no, a closed input and a non-boolean answer write neither file; yes writes the exact IDs and a grant of exactly granted, decidedAt, provider and model. (2) No default: nine answers other than a listed number cancel before any confirmation. (3) The list is exactly the three available models, with no default marker. (4) Committed selection on a new host: confirmation asked once, settings byte-identical after the yes, the grant recorded, and an unchanged rerun reused without asking. A no to that unchanged selection is recorded as this host's decline and reported without asking again. (5) DECLINED CHANGE: with A approved at high, a proposed --thinking low answered no leaves settings and the consent record byte-identical, and the approved selection is still reused without asking; a declined change of model through the flags does the same. (6) Flags: an invalid thinking level, a provider or model alone, an unknown provider and an unavailable model are refused before any prompt, with nothing written. (7) The merge keeps keys Kiln does not own. (8) ROUND TRIP: A to B clears A's grant before B is written and grants B on its own yes. B to A through Kiln asks, and a no leaves B and its grant. A hand edit back to A makes B's grant stale, and the next setup asks for A. (9) Clear before write: a concurrent edit that makes the settings merge refuse still leaves A's grant cleared and the selection unchanged. (10) REFUSED WITHOUT A CLEAR: with Git unavailable, and with the consent record tracked, a change from A to B is refused as grant-not-cleared with settings and the consent record byte-identical. (11) An uninspected host has nothing to choose from. (12) PI'S RULE, OBSERVED: a real inspection of an isolated agent directory with a non-reasoning and a reasoning custom model reports levels off for the first and off, minimal, low, medium, high for the second. (15) A committed high on the non-reasoning model, even with a model-use grant, is reported as unsupported and a level is asked from off only; confirming off persists it. summary: TSK-0042, toward ACC-0060 and ACC-0062 and for TSK-0037's launch check, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit 9f1d427, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. Neither the setup command nor bin/start-kiln.mjs calls these functions yet. THE KEY. lib/compatibility-record.mjs computes all eight determinants from current runtime inputs, never from the stored record: the selection, the model as Pi resolves it, the pinned Pi version, and the EFFECTIVE base URL. Determinant 7 carries the thinking value Pi sends: the model's mapping where it has one, null where it marks the level unsupported, the level itself otherwise, and none for a model that does not reason. Determinant 8 digests the canary protocol as handed to Pi (tool name, description, schema, system prompt, request template with a placeholder challenge, token ceiling, success-predicate version). The package capability signature is not in the key (DEC-0033). R9, THE EFFECTIVE ENDPOINT. Pi can replace a model's baseUrl with one its authentication supplies at request time. resolveEffectiveBaseUrl asks Pi's own authentication resolution with fetch refused; a resolution that would need the network leaves the endpoint unestablished, and then there is no key: setup sends no canary and reports not ready, and launch refuses record reuse (compatibility-uncacheable). R8, THE REQUEST THE CANARY MADE. The canary child resolves its own model from its isolated agent directory, so it reports a bounded projection: the four key fields it computes from its own resolved model and effective endpoint (API type, endpoint identity and source, classified request profile), or a key refusal, and the scheme, host, port and path of each request it sent, observed at fetch. No URL, query, header, credential or unbounded configuration value is reported. proofProblem accepts a pass as proof of a key only when those fields equal the key's, at least one request was observed, and every request lies under the key's endpoint on a path-segment boundary. THE RECORD. Only a passed canary that proves its key is written, and reading and writing both go through the consent record's gate: the ignore block and Git's answer about the record's actual path. A tracked, committed, unignored or unverifiable record is untrusted and never reused (D20). SETUP'S CHECK. lib/live-model-check.mjs reuses a trusted record matching every determinant without asking; otherwise it asks with the section 6.4 prompt naming the provider, the exact model and the possible charge. A run that cannot ask needs --live-model-check approve. deny or a no is a choice: not ready, no request, nothing recorded. A pass that cannot be recorded proves this run only and is reported as awaiting a per-run check, not ready (D21). LAUNCH. lib/launch-checks.mjs's zeroCostPreflight (checks 1 to 6) now also establishes the effective endpoint, and checkLaunch computes the key itself. A different-model one-run override never uses the record, even one matching it, and takes its own approved live check for that run (D17). The project's own selection is proved by a trusted matching record, or refuses to setup (D18); where its record cannot be trusted, each run needs its own check. The canary runner is supplied by the caller (D19). RESULTS. (1) ACC-0060: the prompt names the provider display name, the exact model ID and that the provider may charge, and the canary runs only after the answer. Five declines (false, null, a string, deny, deny with an ask) are choices with no request and no record. A run that cannot ask refuses naming the model and --live-model-check approve; approve runs without asking; with a matching record no flag is needed. (2) ACC-0062: a matching record is reused with nothing asked or sent; a change of provider, model, thinking level, Pi version, API type, endpoint, request profile or canary digest each reopens approval, and declining leaves the record byte-identical. (3) The digest changes with each of its seven parts, ignores key order, and holds exactly those parts. (4) A failed canary, and a runner returning no pass, record nothing and leave an existing record byte-identical. (5) A query-routed endpoint is not checked at all until an identity is declared; with one, the record is keyed declared and holds no query. (6) R9: an unestablishable endpoint sends no canary and, at launch, refuses with no network attempt observed; authentication that supplies a base URL makes that the keyed endpoint, and at launch makes a record taken at the catalogue endpoint mismatch on endpointIdentity. (7) R8: another resolved API type or request profile, a request elsewhere, a request on a sibling path, no observed request and a key refusal in the child each fail the pass in setup and at launch, and nothing is recorded. End to end with the real canary, a child handed a model configuration that does not reason, while the host's does, fails with canary-inputs-differ on effectiveRequestProfile. (8) D20: a force-added record committed and cloned is untrusted in the clone; setup asks again, and launch refuses without a per-run check and passes with one. (9) D21: tracked, unverifiable and unignored locations each leave a pass unrecorded and report awaiting a per-run check, not ready. (10) D17: a stored record matching the override model does not stand in for the override's own approved check. (11) END TO END: the zero-cost preflight, the approved live check with the real canary against a loopback endpoint, then checkLaunch: setup records under the computed key and launch accepts that record with no further request. LIMITS. No billable provider was called; every canary used a loopback endpoint through Pi's openai-completions client. Only fetch-based provider clients are observable; a client that does not use fetch leaves no observed request, which fails the proof rather than passing it. The effective endpoint is established by refusing fetch; a resolution that reached the network another way would not be refused. Wiring into setup (TSK-0060) and into bin/start-kiln.mjs (TSK-0037) is not done, so the criteria are not evaluated. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. summary: TSK-0037, toward ACC-0056 and ACC-0054, measured through the REAL COMMAND. The implementation is commit 4a3ebb7, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. bin/start-kiln.mjs now runs checkLaunch before the supervisor starts anything, and puts what passed on Pi's own command line. It parses --provider, --model and --thinking as the one-run override (each needs a value and may appear once), resolves the project root, and runs the launch checks with that override, a live-canary runner, and an ask only when stdin is a terminal. Pi's agent directory is deliberately NOT resolved first: resolving it loads Pi's SDK, whose bundled debug package enumerates the environment on load, and that is access this host has not yet allowed; the checks ask Pi for the directory only after consent passes. What passed is appended to Pi's argument list as --provider, --model and --thinking (withSelection), which refuses an argument list that already names a model and a selection with nothing usable in it. A refusal prints as a refusal, starts nothing and exits 2, through an exported exitOnFailure the capture fixture also uses, so the fixture ends the way the command does. One typed line is turned into what these modules expect: an explicit yes or no becomes a boolean, a list choice stays a line, and a closed input is null — so an answer the command cannot read is never recorded as a decision, in any phase. A child runs the real command with Node's own fs, environment and network boundaries recorded from before it starts, and every question is recorded with the counts as they stood when it was asked. Loading Pi's SDK enumerates the environment: its bundled `debug` calls Object.keys(process.env) at module load to find its own settings, which was traced to debug/src/node.js inside the Pi bundle rather than inferred. It reads no value, but an enumeration shows which credential variables this computer has, and presence is exactly what this consent gates. The trust store is Pi's and the proposal orders trust before the inspection, so this process cannot both take that decision and stay out of the environment. Masking `process.env` in place does not fix it and was rejected on measurement: hiding a name through a proxy makes the engine verify the omission against the target, which touches the very names being hidden, and building a filtered copy means first seeing which of them exist. A parseable JSON line is not one: the report crosses a process boundary and everything after it acts on the answer, so the state must be one Pi's store can give, the action asked for must be the state that came back, the project must be the one this run is setting up, and the agent directory must be named. The live check writes the compatibility record; a separate phase reads it back and compares it against the key recomputed from what Pi resolved in this run. That is not ceremony: the gate that refuses a tracked or unprotected record applies on READ as well as on write, so a record that cannot be read back is one the next start will refuse, and reporting readiness from the writer's return value would be a promise about somebody else's next run. What the command prints comes from the record that was read. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN REVIEW, AND WHAT THEY WERE (0caaf7b, eeb79bc). FIRST, the canary was given no stored credential path, so its child ran against an empty store: a model Pi authenticates from its saved auth.json would have failed a check that was never handed what makes it work. The request now carries the path, and only when the preflight found the stored file is the source that authenticates this selection — because the canary refuses a stored path that is not there, and an environment-authenticated host commonly has no auth.json at all. Passing it narrows rather than widens: the canary copies the selected provider's entry alone into its isolated root, a boundary measured in test/pi-provider-canary.test.mjs. SECOND, the recovery read trusted a file too early. It is now contained before the first byte — the state root must resolve inside the canonical project root, and the journal inside that as a regular file, so a link on `.pi` or on `.pi/runtime` is refused rather than followed — validated against its schema before any field is used, and never the source of what is printed: the command the operator is told to run is built from this run's own project path. THIRD, that command quoted spaces and printed `C:/a&b/project` bare, which splits a command line in two — and then, on the first correction, used double quotes on Windows, which PowerShell expands: `"C:/a$null/project"` arrives as `C:/a/project`, a different directory with nothing to notice. The command now targets PowerShell explicitly and says so, quoting every path in single quotes with an apostrophe written twice, and the control runs the generated line through that shell against paths holding `$`, a backtick, `&` and an apostrophe, reading back which project the command actually reached. It is recomputed from this run's own project path in every case, never taken from the journal. AN INTERRUPTED RUN IS CONTINUED DELIBERATELY. The journal's presence is the interruption signal. An ordinary rerun names the last completed phase, prints the command to continue — RECOMPUTED FROM THIS RUN'S OWN PROJECT PATH, never the one the interrupted run wrote into its journal — and exits 10 having changed nothing; `--resume` continues, and a completed run leaves no journal. `--resume` with nothing to resume says so and proceeds as an ordinary run. THE EXIT CODES ARE PUBLISHED. `--help` prints every code with what it means, and a test holds each member of the command's own EXIT table to having both a published meaning and a line in that output. This slice adds two: 10 for an interrupted run, and 11 for a model that was not shown to work — which is deliberately distinct from 9, the code for an answer that left setup partial, because a script has to tell a decline from a failure. MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL COMMAND. (1) A zero-cost refusal leaves `live-check` and `read-back` PENDING in the journal the failed run left, with the canary never called. (2) A denied check, a declined one and one nobody could approve each send nothing and record nothing, with the model still committed and the scaffold valid. (3) A passing check is recorded, read back, and reused by the next run: no question, no request, and the record's bytes unchanged. (4) A check that returns not-passed, and one that passes while proving a different endpoint, are both refused with nothing recorded. (5) The read-back itself refuses a record that is gone and one about another model. (6) The interruption, the resume and the no-op resume are all exercised on a real journal. NOTHING BILLABLE IS REACHED, AND THAT IS ENFORCED BY THE FIXTURE. The canary is the single step that sends a request to the selected provider, and the fixture's model is a real OpenAI catalogue entry, so every case injects its own runner; the default — the real canary — is never reached in a test. The injected runner returns what a passing check would have observed, derived from the preflight the command itself resolved, which is also what makes the key comparison meaningful rather than circular. LIMITS. One mutation survives: swallowing a preflight refusal. In this fixture an earlier zero-cost phase refuses first — when the host's stored key goes, its only remaining provider is the loopback one, which has no credential contract — so setup's own tests cannot distinguish a preflight that refuses from one that is ignored. The preflight's individual refusals are held by test/launch-checks.test.mjs. Also unchanged from the earlier slices: R9's alternate content root, custom-provider credential inputs (D25, D13) and `--local-state user` are all still owed, and the spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until they land and the integration record is written. The per-class exit codes are published, but several refusal classes still share the generic setup code; narrowing those is the rest of that mapping. CI. GitHub Actions run 35870095611 at bcfd79a — the slice's final commit — attempt 1 with no job re-run, passed in all four cells, with the setup command's 36 tests running in every cell; the live compatibility tier ran in the ubuntu Node 24 cell and passed 6 of 6. Every earlier commit of the slice passed all four cells too. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Twenty-four changes across five sets, each restored byte-identical by sha256. Twenty-three were caught: the read-back skipped, a not-ready check reported as ready, a declined check and a failed one sharing a code, an unapproved check assumed approved, the canary given no preflight, an interrupted run continued without being asked, the read-back accepting a record about another model, the read-back accepting an unreadable record, the canary given no saved credential, the canary handed the wrong store, the journal read without containment, a non-file at the journal path read, the journal used unvalidated, the printed recovery command taken from the file, a path with spaces left unquoted, the state root not checked against the project, quoting applied only to paths that look awkward, POSIX given Windows quoting, a stored path supplied whatever authenticates, no stored path supplied at all, Windows given double quotes that PowerShell expands inside, an apostrophe left undoubled there, and a printed line that names no shell. THE ONE THAT SURVIVES is swallowing a preflight refusal, for the reason stated above.
