summary: TSK-0060 SLICE 5, which closes the four things the earlier slices owed: R9's alternate content root, `--local-state user`, the custom-provider credential inputs (D25, D13) and the per-class exit codes. The implementation is commits 0a325c7, 2c61a1b and 804dd43; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. R9. The initializer now takes an explicit content root, contained inside the project, and stages its scaffold BESIDE the destination rather than in the project root — a rename is only atomic within one filesystem, and the destination is where the filesystem in question is. Setup passes the resolved content root instead of refusing every non-default selection, and prints that later runs need the same selection, since only that selection finds the content again. The skill-override entry was already derived and proved; what was missing was a command that could reach a project where the derivation differs from the default. MEASURED: content selected at `kiln-content` is initialized there, no second root appears beside it, `../kiln-content/skills-overrides` is committed, and Pi's own loader finds an override placed in that directory. A content root outside the project, or the project itself, is refused; the staging location is asserted through the initializer's rename seam, with a NESTED content root, because for a root directly under the project "beside the destination" and "in the project root" are the same directory and the difference would be invisible. `--local-state user`. The external root is keyed by the project's committed id and never by its path: a path-derived root moves the moment somebody renames the project, taking every transcript and consent record with it. A project that has an id resolves from its record; a fresh one commits the id first, in a transaction planning that record alone and opening no journal — because the journal lives in the root being resolved. What can honestly be printed before any mutation is the rule; the exact path follows the moment the id makes it knowable, and before any runtime data exists. MEASURED: consent and compatibility records land under the per-user root keyed by the committed id, `.pi/runtime` is never created in the project, and no machine-specific session path is committed to settings. D25, THE CUSTOM PROVIDER. Kiln's table holds the built-in credential contracts; a provider Pi knows and Kiln does not needs the operator to say which environment variable carries its key. `--credential-var NAME` is that input, and without it such a provider is refused rather than bound to, because a contract Kiln invented would be a guess about somebody's credential. A NAME, NEVER A VALUE: a key on the command line is a key in the shell history and in every process listing, so the flag takes the variable's name — and the refusal for anything else does not repeat what was given, in case it is the credential itself. That refusal WAS leaking it, and a control caught it before this landed. The canary's child also needs to know where a custom provider is, which is not a credential: the base URL, the API kind and the one model, taken from what the preflight resolved so the check and the record describe the same request. Without it the child resolves the id against Pi's built-in catalogue and checks a different service. THE REAL CANARY, THROUGH THE WHOLE COMMAND, AGAINST AN ENDPOINT THIS TEST SERVES. One case runs setup with no injected canary at all, against a provider defined in the fixture's `models.json` and pointed at a loopback server: undeclared, the run refuses and the endpoint is never contacted; declared, it resumes from the journal the refusal left, the canary makes exactly ONE request, the recorded key names 127.0.0.1, neither the key nor its variable's name appears in anything written, and the next run reuses the record without a second request. THE EXIT CODES. Every Kiln refusal class shared the generic setup code, which tells a script that "choose a model", "this provider needs a credential declaration" and "the package entry could not be written" are one situation. Five codes join the table: selection, credentials, registration, research and unusable. The ignore owner's refusals map to state protection, which is the failure they are, and the live check's approval refusal stays with the partial-setup code, because it is an answer rather than a fault. A class the table does not name keeps the generic code rather than being guessed at. `--help` publishes all sixteen, and the control holds each class to its code, each code to a published meaning AND a line in that output, and the unnamed case to falling through. Four classes are also proved through the real command; the three it cannot currently reach are named in the test so the table is not a list of aspirations. LIMITS. The spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until the integrated record. A non-default content root is supported by setup, and every later run must carry the same `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR` selection to find it — which is printed, not assumed. Nothing here proves a real provider: the one real canary in this slice answers to a loopback server this test runs, and every other case injects its runner. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Eighteen changes across four sets, each restored byte-identical by sha256, and ALL eighteen were caught: the selected content root ignored, a content root outside the project accepted, the scaffold staged in the project root again, external state written into the project, the external root keyed by something other than the id, the path rule not printed before the id exists, a custom provider needing no declaration, the declaration never reaching the preflight, the canary told nothing about the provider, the canary pointed at a different endpoint, a value accepted where a name belongs, every refusal sharing the generic code again, the selection class mapped to the wrong code, a credential refusal reading as a registration one, an unnamed class guessed at, a code published with no meaning, and the two staging and containment cases above. TWO OF THESE SURVIVED THEIR FIRST RUN and were killed only after the controls were sharpened: the containment refusal had no test at all, and the staging assertion could not tell the two places apart until the fixture used a nested content root.

summary: TSK-0060, INTEGRATED. The ordered setup command, measured end to end through `main()` against real projects, for the six criteria that span the whole command. The implementation is everything from e808b96 to 7fd92da; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. ACC-0085, THE PATHS BEFORE THE FIRST LASTING WRITE. A project-local run prints the canonical tool root, project root, content root, settings path and runtime state path in its first five lines, and the install seam captures the project tree at the moment the bootstrap ran: byte-identical to its pre-run state. An EXTERNAL run is the harder case, because a per-user root is keyed by the project's committed id — so the id is derived in memory, the exact path is printed, and the identity phase is handed THAT id to commit. Measured in a child with every filesystem call recorded from before the command starts: the line naming the external path is printed after ZERO writes to the project, and the id in it is the id the run then committed. A `--project-root` that disagrees with the resolved content owner refuses with both printed, having written nothing. ACC-0106, NO SECRET AND NO ABSOLUTE PATH IN WHAT IS COMMITTED. A complete run against an environment-authenticated provider — asserted from the preflight's own line, since a stored credential would be a different arrangement — with research enabled and its connection checked. The file set is what THIS RUN added or changed: git's own answer before and after, NUL-delimited so a newline in a path cannot read as two entries, with the rename form handled — rather than a list written in the test that would pass forever while the command grew a file nobody added to it. A file the operator writes before the run, carrying a key and a path of its own, is not in that set, which is how the boundary is observable rather than merely intended. Each file is read and asserted to carry no credential, nothing derived from one (sha256 in hex and base64, base64 of the key, a prefix of it), no authorisation header, no path belonging to this machine, and not even the NAMES of the credential variables. `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are asserted by name to be in that set; the ignored consent and compatibility records are asserted not to be. EVERY entry in that set is read: there is no exemption list, and an entry that is not a regular file fails, because passing over what a scan cannot read is how a scan stops being one. The fixture's `.planning` link is not in the set at all — it is in the before and the after alike. Absolute paths are checked by shape as well as by value, which is what catches the likeliest real leak: a generator interpolating the checkout it was run from. ONE THING THE SCAN CANNOT PROVE BY DELETION. Removing the leak scan's assertions fails nothing, because nothing currently leaks — a scan bites when there is something to find. What proves it works is injecting leaks: a credential variable's name in settings, an absolute path in a generated document, and the research key in the project record are each caught. ACC-0107, ONE IDENTITY AND THE STATE LIBRARY'S OWN CHOICES. The id is minted once and reused, with the journal gone when the run completes. A project with no coverage is shown exactly the three choices the state library returns, with the ignore block's own bytes; answering nothing, `stop`, `user-state` or anything unrecognised stops with nothing written; and a non-interactive run refuses on the same object with no `.pi`, no content root and no ignore file. External state is offered, which AST-0047 (on EVD-0081) permits: pi 0.84.4 relocates session transcripts through `--session-dir` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, so the per-user root is reachable without committing an absolute path — and a run in that mode commits no `sessionDir` at all. ACC-0043, BYTE-IDENTICAL ON A RERUN. A second run naming nothing reads back the committed selection and this host's approval of it, asks no question, and leaves every file byte-identical — the whole tree by digest, not a reported status — including the settings file, the ignore block, the identity file and the generated content. A third run leaves `.pi/kiln.json`'s mtime untouched, so nothing is rewritten with identical bytes. The compatibility record is byte-identical too, and the check is not run again. ACC-0045, BOTH INTERRUPTION WINDOWS, BY KILLING A RUN. Inside the bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists: a real child is killed mid-install, the project is byte-identical afterwards, no `.pi` survives, and an ordinary rerun — no `--resume`, because there is nothing to resume — completes. After the journal opens: a real child is killed during the trust phase, and what it left records the phase IN FLIGHT as running, which is only true because that status is written before the work; the journal carries an exact resume command naming this project, and the arguments are PARSED OUT OF THAT COMMAND rather than typed beside it — so a command naming another project, omitting `--resume`, or absent altogether each fail the control — and running them completes the remaining phases and leaves no journal. A failure in an agent phase leaves the scaffold: a declined inspection, an unconfirmed model, a denied or failed live check each report partial setup with the project valid. THAT MEASUREMENT FOUND A DEFECT, IN BOTH WINDOWS. A killed run leaves its lockfile, and the stale window that protects waiters from a slow holder is two minutes — so every rerun after a kill refused for two minutes on a lock held by a process that no longer exists. Setup now clears such a lock before any run waits on it, and the safety is in what it still refuses: another machine's lock, an unreadable one, and one whose pid is alive are each left where they are, so two live setups exclude each other exactly as before. REVIEW FOUND A SECOND DEFECT IN THAT FIX, THE CONTROL WRITTEN FOR THE SECOND FOUND A THIRD, AND REVIEW OF THAT FIX FOUND A FOURTH. All four are one mistake at four depths: judging a file and then removing it, when what was judged can be replaced in between. Clearing a dead owner's lock by read-then-unlink lets two recoveries both acquire, and every rerun took that path. Claiming the lock by rename instead — atomic, so only one recovery wins — moves a lock that went live in the meantime, and although the re-judge puts it back, a waiter creates its own over the free name while it is gone; four racing recoveries caught exactly that in CI on their first run. So removing somebody else's lock is now SERIALISED rather than made atomic: a breaker takes a gate beside the lock and judges inside it, where a lockfile cannot turn from a dead owner's into a live one's — creating one requires it to be absent, making it absent requires removing it, and the only removers are its own holder, dead by assumption, and a breaker, which is here. Both break paths take the gate, the recovery's and the waiter's stale break, because either alone leaves the window. AND THE GATE HAD THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL DOWN, TWICE: two reclaimers could both find one abandoned gate old and ownerless, and the second would clear a gate the first was already holding. Reclaiming is therefore serialised too, by a token only one process can create, and the judgement that acts is made under it. AND JUDGING IT BY AGE WAS ITSELF WRONG. Taking the gate and writing the owner record into it are two calls, and a process can be stopped between them for as long as the operating system likes — suspended, paged out, held at a breakpoint — so an old EMPTY gate says only that somebody created it, never that they died. What is reclaimed now is a gate whose record names a process on this host that is demonstrably gone, and nothing else: an unreadable one, or one naming another machine, fails closed with both paths named, because it will never clear itself and a silent pass would strand every later run on a timeout about a pid. That case is measured against a real process stopped in exactly that window: its gate is old and empty, the run refuses by name rather than taking it, and the stopped process then carries on and releases the gate itself. THE TOKEN IS THE END OF THE CHAIN, BECAUSE NOTHING RECLAIMS IT: a token left behind by a process killed inside those few calls stops automatic breaking altogether, and the command refuses with exit code 17, naming both files to remove. Fail closed with a route out is the last link; guessing would be a fifth defect of the same shape. Controls: four racing recoveries; two reclaimers and a waiter racing from an abandoned gate; a second breaker and a waiter each refusing to clear a lock somebody else is clearing; a gate that is old but whose holder is alive left alone; a real process stopped between taking its gate and naming itself keeping that gate; an old unreadable gate and one from another machine each refusing; a gate whose record names a dead local process reclaimed; an abandoned token refusing; and the command's refusal naming both paths, followed by the same command completing once they are removed. Thirteen mutations across the three rounds are caught. ONE IS NOT, AND IT IS DECLARED: removing the re-judge under the token survives, because the state it defends against — a previous reclaimer finishing between this one's two looks — cannot be produced without an interleaving, so only the racing controls cover it, and controls of exactly that kind are what found the third and fourth defects. ACC-0108, TRUST OBTAINED AND NEVER ASSUMED. An interactive run prints the canonical project directory the decision applies to and asks; `--trust approve` records an approval with no prompt and answers over a recorded decision; a run with nobody to ask refuses WITHOUT REACHING THE QUESTION, measured as zero questions asked. Only an explicit yes approves and only an explicit no denies — a closed input, an empty line and an unreadable answer each leave the store with no decision. A denial is reported as not ready, the agent is never described as usable, nothing is registered, the journal is removed, the scaffold that survives is put through Kiln's own plan linter rather than declared valid because its files exist, AND THE BROWSER-ONLY ROUTE IS SERVED: the application is started against that denied project and asked for a page, which returns a rendered document. Content that validates does not establish that a server can read it. An unapproved project loads none of the package's tools, which is the same fact from Pi's side. WHAT THE WHOLE COMMAND DOES, IN ONE SENTENCE PER PHASE, IS IN THE SLICE RECORDS: EVD-0133 (the order, the built-ins-only graph, the locked install), EVD-0134 (the pinned runtime, trust, registration), EVD-0135 (consent before any read, discovery, selection, the credential contract, research), EVD-0136 (the zero-cost preflight, the separately approved live check, the read-back) and EVD-0137 (the selected content root, the per-user root, the declared custom provider, the exit codes). LIMITS. Nothing billable is contacted anywhere: the one real canary in the suite answers to a loopback server the test runs, every other case injects its runner, the research probe answers through an injected adapter, and npm is a seam in every case — what the bootstrap does is asserted by its arguments, its confinement and the lockfile digest either side. `ACC-0108`'s browser-only route is served for real, but only as this application serving a page: `npm start`'s production path, which installs and builds first, is not exercised. The canary's real request against a real provider, and a real `npm ci` against a registry, remain outside this suite by design.

summary: TSK-0061, THE ARGUMENT SURFACE AND THE NON-INTERACTIVE CONTRACT. What this task's three open notes asked for, measured through `bin/setup.mjs` itself. The implementation is 4f07b18, 85ed347 and 9c16cdd; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. MODEL USE, CONFIRMED BY A RUN WITH NOBODY TO ASK. A model is used only after an explicit confirmation (EVD-0128), and a fresh non-interactive run could not obtain one, so it could never finish. `--model-use approve|deny` is that same answer given in advance: the confirmation text is printed in full before either answer is applied, because the prompt is where the billing is disclosed and a flag that skipped the words would authorise ongoing charges with nothing saying so in the terminal or the log. IT CONFIRMS, IT DOES NOT CHOOSE: a run that names no model still refuses, and `--non-interactive` alone confirms nothing. A SECOND ANSWER WAS MISSING AND IS NOW HERE TOO: the inspection question had no non-interactive answer either, so such a run stopped before the model phase ever ran; `--inspect approve|deny` settles it, and only an explicit value does. A complete run is now `--non-interactive --inspect approve --provider X --model Y --thinking Z --model-use approve`, which asks nothing, commits the selection and records the grant; `--model-use deny` reads the same disclosure, records nothing and leaves a valid project. DECLARED IDENTITIES, AS INPUTS AND AS THE PROJECT'S. A model whose endpoint cannot be canonicalised, or whose request depends on values Kiln may neither persist nor hash, has no compatibility key without a non-secret identity somebody declares (D22). `--endpoint-identity` is checked by `canonicalizeEndpoint` — the one canonicaliser, moved to a built-ins-only module so an argument is still checked before anything is installed or written — and `--request-identity` by the pattern its own schema declares, with a test holding the two spellings equal. BOTH ARE COMMITTED TO `.pi/kiln.json`, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THEM USABLE AT ALL: the key is recomputed at every setup and every launch, so a declaration living only on the command line that first supplied it would leave the next run recomputing a different key and refusing the record it had just written. Measured end to end against a loopback endpoint with the real canary: without the identity the run reports not ready and sends nothing; with it the canary runs once and the record carries `{categories: [samplingParams], declaredIdentity: acme-gateway-v3}` and none of the configuration's own values; a later run naming no identity reuses the record; changing the label is a different request and is not reused. AND AT LAUNCH. `bin/start-kiln.mjs` now passes the project's committed declarations to `checkLaunch`, which is the same key recomputed a second time. The control runs the real launch checks against the project setup proved: they pass by reusing the record, with the declaration removed from the committed record they refuse, and the launcher is shown handing the committed value through. REFUSALS THAT REPEAT NOTHING. An operator who pastes a key into the wrong option has already put it in their shell history; a refusal that echoed it would spread it to a terminal, a log and a CI transcript. Every option with a fixed set of answers now names the answers instead, the endpoint canonicaliser no longer quotes the URL it was given, and a key-shaped sentinel through all eight options — and through the real command with the whole help printed after it — appears nowhere. AND A DECLARED IDENTITY IN THE SHAPE OF A KEY IS REFUSED BEFORE IT IS PRINTED, COMMITTED OR HASHED. A label is published by design, so the mistake worth catching is the common one: an issuer prefix, a JWT, a long opaque token, the same beside a word, or a token routed as a path segment in an endpoint. Through the real command the refusal happens as an argument check — no install, no scaffold, no `.pi`, the project byte-identical — and the value is not repeated. HELP. `--help` documents every option, and says in the words every user-disabled research outcome carries (EVD-0127) that research is turned on by running setup again with `--research tavily`. ACC-0084, EVERY CLASS THIS COMMAND CAN RAISE. Twenty scenarios are driven through `main()` and the code each returns is compared with what `--help` publishes: a value the command cannot read, an unknown option, a credential where a variable name belongs, an endpoint identity carrying credentials, a project root that does not own the content, an install that is not the pin, a bootstrap that could not complete, a repository that does not ignore the runtime paths with nobody to ask, a settings file somebody broke, a package entry that cannot be proved, a project nobody trusts, a refused look at this computer, an interrupted run nobody chose to continue, a provider Kiln has no contract for, research that cannot be turned back on safely because a colleague committed the consent record, a recovery whose files only the operator may remove, a computer with no provider connected, a model named but never confirmed, a billable check the operator refused, a model that did not pass the check, and a model this computer declined. Scenarios are grouped by class, so several bad arguments are one code while two different instructions may not share one. AUTHENTICATION BECAME ITS OWN CLASS while doing this: "connect a provider in Pi" cannot be answered by rerunning with flags, and arriving as the selection code would have a script retry forever, so it is exit 18. LIMITS, EACH ONE A BOUNDARY OF WHAT WAS MEASURED. (1) A SHAPE CHECK IS NOT A SECRET DETECTOR. What is refused is a credential in a shape somebody issues; a secret in no recognised shape is accepted, and `--request-identity` is committed and printed by design. "Bounded" is not "non-secret", and nothing here establishes that an accepted label is safe to publish. (2) THE CUSTOM-PROVIDER CONTROL REACHES `checkLaunch`, NOT A STARTED PROCESS. `bin/start-kiln.mjs` cannot start a custom-provider project at all: it has no input for the credential declaration `--credential-var` gives setup, so the launch refuses with `unsupported-credential-contract`. That gap predates these flags and is TSK-0037's (D2); no project in this record should be read as "starts". (3) `EXIT.UNUSABLE` AND LAUNCH FAILURE ARE NOT OBSERVED THROUGH SETUP. The selection phase refuses first in every case that would reach the preflight's `LaunchRefusal`. Setup publishes `EXIT.UNUSABLE`, which the matrix checks, and has no separate launch-failure code. The test declares the boundary rather than leaving it to be inferred. ACC-0084 was amended on the strength of that: it no longer names either class, and covers `bin/setup.mjs` alone. What raises them is the combined runtime supervisor, and a criterion against CMP-0037 for its own refusal classes and codes is owed and recorded there and on TSK-0037 — so nothing yet claims those codes are distinct or published. (4) NOTHING BILLABLE IS CONTACTED. The one real canary answers to a loopback server this suite runs; every other case injects its runner, the research probe is an injected adapter, and npm is a seam. (5) A BUILT-IN PROVIDER'S UNBOUNDED CONFIGURATION STILL CANNOT BE PROVED, AND FAILS CLOSED. A custom provider's non-credential configuration crosses into the canary's isolated directory, so the child makes the request this project makes; a built-in provider's does not, so the child's key cannot be computed, `proofProblem` answers `canary-key-unavailable`, and nothing is recorded. Controlled as a refusal rather than worked around. WHAT PROVES THE CONTROLS BITE. THIRTEEN mutations across three rounds, each caught, and they are named here so the count can be checked against the list rather than taken on trust: the standing answer applied without printing what it authorises; `--non-interactive` alone confirming; a refusal appending the value it refused; the canonicaliser quoting what it was given; the declaration never committed; the launcher handing no declarations; the canary child deprived of the sampling parameters; an unauthenticated computer reported as a selection problem; the help dropping what re-enables research; the credential guard disabled, skipped for path segments, examining only whole values, or moved after the write. That is thirteen. A FOURTEENTH WAS ATTEMPTED AND DOES NOT COUNT: it changed a refusal helper's signature without using the new parameter, so it altered no behaviour and failed nothing, which is a defect in the mutation rather than a gap in the controls. It was rewritten to append the refused value for real — that rewrite is the third in the list — and a no-op is reported here rather than counted as a pass.
title: Measurement: the setup command's argument surface, its non-interactive consent contract, and the declared identities it commits for setup and launch

summary: TSK-0062, COMPONENT WORK ONLY. It does not evaluate ACC-0086, which needs TSK-0063's journey from an empty directory. The fixture is `test/helpers/provider-fixture.mjs`, commit 702ee9c. It is a provider bound to 127.0.0.1 that answers `/v1/chat/completions` in the streamed shape Pi's `openai-completions` client reads, and `modelsJson()` names it as `kiln-fixture/fixture-model` with its key as a `$KILN_FIXTURE_PROVIDER_KEY` reference. DETERMINISTIC. Every id and timestamp in a reply is fixed, and the scripted step that answers is chosen by the number of assistant messages after the last user message, not by how many requests came before. Two identical requests got byte-identical replies, and a second user turn started the script again. IT CANNOT LOOP. Past the end of its script every reply is prose, so a tool call is issued once and is not re-issued because its triggering text is still in the conversation. THROUGH THE PINNED RUNTIME. Pi's `ModelRegistry` listed the model and reported configured authentication only with the key variable set (the control, without it, listed neither). Pi's own CLI, in print mode with only the `read` tool, sent two authorised requests: the fixture's `read` call was executed, the file's sentinel reached the provider in the tool message, the closing prose was in Pi's output, and Pi exited 0. Kiln's live canary passed through it, with the fixture echoing the challenge from the request. CONTROLS. A missing or wrong key is refused with 401, a non-streamed request with 400, any other route with 404, and the key is never recorded. A mutation that forced every request to the first step failed the conversation test and the CLI test; the CLI run is bounded at 60 seconds, so a looping regression fails instead of hanging the suite. The canary still passed under that mutation, because the canary stops after one call of its own. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. No Kiln project was started against the fixture, because `bin/start-kiln.mjs` cannot start a custom-provider project (now TSK-0072, a prerequisite of TSK-0063). No Stage 1 exchange was driven through it; that is TSK-0063's.

summary: TSK-0072, toward ACC-0116, which is left not-evaluated for review. The implementation is c3c8fd0 (a mechanical move of canaryRequest and its custom-provider config to lib/launch-checks.mjs), 8ab0b16 (the TSK-0062 fixture) and 1d0ee30. WHERE THE DECLARATION LIVES. Setup's `--credential-var` NAME is now written to this host's consent record, as `modelUse.credentialVar`, beside the grant for exactly that provider and model and only when that grant says yes. It is never committed: `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` do not carry it. A model or provider change clears the grant and the declaration with it. The schema admits a variable name only. THE LAUNCH. After the model-use grant stands, `zeroCostPreflight` reads the declaration for the recorded selection and resolves the same custom contract setup proved; a one-run override of the model has no grant and so no declaration. When a one-run canary is needed, `checkLaunch` passes the declaration and the provider's non-credential configuration to it. MEASURED THROUGH BOTH REAL COMMANDS, against the TSK-0062 fixture. Setup with `--credential-var` ran the real canary once and completed. A second setup run named no variable, reused the declaration and the record, and made no request. The real `bin/start-kiln.mjs`, with its real launch checks and only its supervisor replaced by a recorder, passed on this computer's record with Pi held to `--provider kiln-fixture --model fixture-model --thinking off`, and made no request. With the declared variable empty the same launch exited 2, refused as `No authentication is configured for kiln-fixture fixture-model`, and started nothing. CONTROL. With launch's derivation of the declaration disabled, the ACC-0116 case failed. A FINDING ON THE WAY. The fixture's `models.json` first set `compat`, and setup refused it with `canary-inputs-differ`: the canary accepts only baseUrl, api and models for a custom provider, so a `compat` block changes the parent's request and not the child's. That fails closed. The fixture no longer sets `compat` (8ab0b16), and a custom provider that needs `compat` still cannot pass setup.

summary: TSK-0072, toward ACC-0116, which is left not-evaluated for review. It supersedes EVD-0141's design, which the review of 1d0ee30 rejected on four findings. The implementation is 8db3f35 and fc7d72b, with the schema wording in 19e487c. F11, CONFIRMED WITH THE MODEL. For a custom provider the declared variable is part of the model-use choice. Setup's confirmation prints "Key from: the environment variable NAME" before the operator answers, and the grant is recorded with that name. A different variable for the same model makes the old grant stale: it is cleared and asked for again. The silent writer EVD-0141 described (recordCredentialVar) is removed. Launch does not know the name, so its grant check does not compare it; it reads the name from the grant. F12, KEPT OR REFUSED. Before the live check, setup refuses (exit 13, declaration-not-remembered) unless this host's grant stands granted and carries exactly the declared name. Measured by setting up a project, then tracking its consent record in Git: the rerun refused, and the provider received no second request. F13, PI'S ROUTE. After consent, setup and launch both read Pi's models.json for the selected provider and refuse unless its apiKey is a reference to exactly the declared variable. Setup refuses with exit 13 (declared-route-mismatch), before the preflight, so EXIT.UNUSABLE stays unobserved through setup as EVD-0139 states. Launch refuses with exit 2 (credential-route-mismatch). The refusal carries a code (different-variable, not-a-variable, provider-absent, models-unreadable) and never a value: with a literal key in models.json, the key appears nowhere in the output. F14, STARTS. test/custom-provider-start.test.mjs replaces nothing. Real setup runs as a process with --credential-var against TSK-0062's fixture. Then the real bin/start-kiln.mjs runs its launch checks, which pass on the record for kiln-fixture fixture-model (thinking off). It starts the real shell, which is identity-confirmed ready, and the real pinned Pi. Pi's input is a pipe: on the pinned Pi, with no TTY, it reads its input to the end and runs it as one prompt. The one line written reached the fixture as one authorised request for fixture-model, offering Kiln's tools, including kiln_project_status. Pi printed the provider's answer and exited 0. The supervisor reported "stopped (agent-exit)" with the launcher tree stopped, the command exited 0, and nothing answered on its port afterwards. The run holds the .next build lock and is bounded at five minutes. CONTROLS. Five mutations, each failing its case, with every file restored byte-identically: the variable dropped from the staleness rule (F11); the keep check disabled (F12); setup's route check disabled (F13); launch's route check disabled (F13); launch's reading of the declaration disabled (F14, the real start).

summary: TSK-0058, toward ACC-0103's start-prompt clause, which EVD-0110 did not measure. PROBE FIRST, ON THE PINNED 0.84.4. Pi was started with the supervisor's own argument list plus a positional /kiln-start, after real setup against TSK-0062's loopback fixture. Interactive, under a util-linux script pseudo-terminal in WSL Ubuntu 24.04 on Node 24.11.0: the provider received one authorised request whose only user message was Pi's expansion of kiln-start.md, and typing /quit exited 0. Print mode with empty input (Windows, Node 24.18.0, and WSL): the same single expanded turn. A fresh project and an agent directory with nothing authenticated; setup run with --trust approve --inspect approve --provider openai --model gpt-4o --thinking off --model-use approve --live-model-check deny --research disabled, so nothing could reach OpenAI. Keys were synthetic input events sent only to the verified foreground window. BEFORE PI OPENED, setup printed that no provider is authenticated, to type /login and then /quit, that nothing typed in Pi is recorded by setup, and that Pi uses its own agent directory, named in full, which setup does not isolate, may download helper programs into it, and /login may change Pi's own default provider and model there, while the project's model is chosen by setup afterwards. Pi then opened interactive, in a temporary kiln-login directory, with the login flags present on its process; it downloaded fd and ripgrep into the agent directory, as disclosed. CONNECTED: /login, Sign in with an API key, OpenAI, a throwaway key. Pi saved it to the agent directory's auth.json (openai: api_key) and set its own default model there. After /quit setup printed Pi closed (exit 0); looking at this computer again, found the provider, confirmed the model by --model-use approve, passed its zero-cost preflight, and stopped at the declined live check: exit 9, partial, nothing sent to the provider. The temporary directory was removed. CLOSED WITHOUT A LOGIN: the same run with nothing authenticated, /quit at once. Setup printed Pi closed (exit 0); looking at this computer again, that Pi was closed and still no provider is authenticated, and reason: no-available-models, and exited 18 (the authentication code). auth.json stayed {}. That Pi's input and output were inherited and nothing of the session captured is the launch code's (stdio inherit, no log), asserted by the TSK-0068 test that also fixes the exact pinned command, flags, agent directory and removed working directory; this observation shows the TUI owning the terminal.
